title: Share hysteresis storage across the 32 agree predictions
motivation:
The retained r4s2 predictor uses 32 private two-bit counters and a seven-bit
training queue. It improved bracketed cycles by 1.48%, but most of its
fitness gain came from routed Fmax. The r5s2 expansion saved only 0.14%
of scored cycles while losing 26.40% of Fmax; r6s2 history indexing added
0.20% cycles and lost 25.74% of Fmax. These results favor investigating
predictor compaction while retaining all 32 direction entries and their
fixed PC hash. Confidence storage is a narrower opportunity than changing
the accepted-fetch path or partitioning each branch's training by history.

hypothesis.motivation:
The retained r4s2 predictor uses 32 private two-bit counters and a seven-bit
training queue. It improved bracketed cycles by 1.48%, but most of its
fitness gain came from routed Fmax. The r5s2 expansion saved only 0.14%
of scored cycles while losing 26.40% of Fmax; r6s2 history indexing added
0.20% cycles and lost 25.74% of Fmax. These results favor investigating

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the 32 independent two-bit agree counters with 32 private
agreement-prediction bits and eight shared hysteresis bits. Each fixed
group of four consecutive table entries shares one hysteresis bit:
group = index[4:2]. Preserve the existing module ports, five-bit PC hash,
seven-bit registered training queue, and single 32-to-1 prediction-bit
lookup. This is one predictor-storage change; it introduces no history
register, additional prediction bank, target cache, or pipeline metadata.

Represent each entry's prediction by P[index], where 1 predicts agreement
with the instruction's backward-taken/forward-not-taken bias. H[group]=1
means strong confidence and H[group]=0 means weak confidence. Reset all
P and H bits to 1. When a previously queued valid training event drains,
let i be its index, g=i[4:2], and A its actual agreement. Compute both
updates from pre-edge state:
  P[i] next = H[g] ? P[i] : A
  H[g] next = (P[i] == A)
Hold every other P bit and every unrelated H bit. In particular, H uses
the old P[i], not its newly assigned value. This produces the ordinary
two-bit saturating prediction transitions for an entry trained in
isolation. Sharing permits another entry in its group to change its
confidence, but never directly changes that entry's prediction bit.

Keep prediction reads dependent only on P[lookup_index]; H must not enter
the fetch-direction cone. Use generated, constant-index local updates
for P. Implement each group's hysteresis update from only that group's
four prediction bits and the queued event, using a small local selection
or masked reduction. Do not introduce a dynamic 32-entry training read,
a global selected-counter feedback path, or a combinational EX bypass.
Qualify group updates with the queued validity and matching group index.
The intended storage reduction is exactly 24 predictor state bits:
64 counter bits become 40 prediction/confidence bits, with the seven
queue bits unchanged. Confirm the mapped LUT and FF cost rather than
assuming the group-update logic also reduces LUT count.

Preserve the existing event capture and drain schedule. Capture EX
training validity on every clock, and drain the previous event even when
no new event arrives or fetch/EX is held. Reset cancels pending events
and overrides updates. Consecutive events, including events sharing a
group, consume the latest registered P/H state without being merged or
dropped. Fetch accepted on an update edge uses the pre-edge prediction;
its saved pred_taken remains authoritative for later mismatch detection.
Existing legal, nontrapping EX-advance qualification, stall and recovery
priorities, aligned direct-target generation, and JAL/JALR behavior stay
intact. Prediction errors continue to recover through the existing EX
mechanism; architectural targets, traps, side effects, and RVFI remain
independent of predictor confidence.

The estimate is 2% higher fitness with low confidence, not a measurement.
The proposed benefit is lower predictor storage and update cost while
retaining direction capacity and fetch latency. Shared confidence can
cause extra recoveries, and whole-core mapping can worsen despite fewer
state bits; neither unchanged cycles nor improved Fmax is guaranteed.
Compare bracketed cycles and three-seed median routed Fmax separately,
then compute fitness using unrounded iterations/cycle. Run the unchanged
correctness and fitness gates, preserving nret=1 and every hard invariant.
Verify the requested 6 KB CRCs, timing markers, completion text, and memory
bounds. Prior notes distinguish a 2 KB scored ELF from supplemental 6 KB
validation: record the actual workload and compare like with like without
changing either workload or any evaluation file.

Implemented the shared-hysteresis hypothesis exactly in
`cores/bench/rtl/branch_predictor.sv`. The 32 private two-bit counters are
now 32 private prediction bits and eight confidence bits, grouped by
index[4:2]. Both reset to one. Generated constant-index entry updates use
the old group confidence; each generated group selects only its four
prediction bits and compares the selected OLD prediction with the queued
actual agreement. Nonblocking assignments preserve the specified old-state
semantics when prediction and confidence change together.

The seven registered event bits, unconditional validity capture, previous
event drain, reset cancellation, module ports, fixed PC hash, and single
32-to-1 prediction lookup are preserved. No other RTL changed. There is
no confidence input to the fetch lookup, dynamic 32-entry training read,
EX bypass, history, additional bank, or pipeline metadata. The core remains
nret=1, with its existing legality, targets, traps, forwarding, stall and
recovery priorities, JAL/JALR behavior, side effects, and RVFI contract.

The predictor reference model now decodes P/H into an ordinary saturating
counter, advances it arithmetically, and re-encodes direction and strength.
Unit coverage checks all eight state/outcome transitions for every isolated
entry, endpoints, consecutive events, all groups and local selectors,
cross-entry confidence interference, unchanged untrained predictions,
unrelated groups, disabled capture with pending drain, cancellation, event
accounting, randomized sequences, and pre-edge reads. IF coverage retains
the existing legality/alignment/full-width target assertions and adds both
static biases, neighbor-only confidence changes, and both direction changes
coincident with acceptance or a fetch hold. The pipeline scoreboard checks
all P/H bits and queued events every cycle while retaining full ISS/RVFI
comparison, retirement order, PC chaining, memory transactions, exactly-once
EX training, and all prior architectural assertions. New programs exercise
distinct entries sharing only confidence, stale accepted predictions,
load-to-branch forwarding, recovery during imem stalls, and wrong-path work.

with a true dmem pipeline hold in this core, because that already-advanced
branch itself occupies EX/MEM on its drain cycle. The new directed test
drives dmemReady low during the pending drain, then holds the following
store for four clocks with a younger branch frozen, checking no replay or
duplicate training. Existing divider-hold draining and IF-hold update tests

state.

title: Make multiplier sharing explicit with registered signedness
motivation:
Repeated experiments expose binary ALU-control paths to EX/MEM after
relatively small whole-design changes. The r1s0 full one-hot conversion
improved its original baseline timing but added 404 LUT4 and left the
registered MULHU selector critical. The r2s1 multiplier pipeline reduced
Fmax and added dependency cycles while ALU selection remained critical.
This motivates a narrower change to multiply-mode control at the existing
stage boundaries.

Inspection of the retained r4s2 synthesis log shows that Yosys already
merges mul_ss, mul_su, and mul_uu into one MULT36X36. Its resource-sharing
activation expressions include ALU opcode comparisons, div_wait, and
div_consume. Three source-level multiplications therefore do not imply
three physical multipliers. Explicit operand signedness and a common high
result can simplify this inferred sharing and selection network without
changing instruction latency. The retained winner's worst routed paths
end in ID/EX operand captures, so this is a control-cone hypothesis, not
evidence that its current critical path traverses the multiplier.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Express all four multiply instructions with one signed 33-by-33 product
whose two operand-extension controls are decoded before ID/EX. Add only
mul_signed_a and mul_signed_b to id_ex_t. Decode them from the existing
validated decoder's dec_alu_op: MULH sets both, MULHSU sets only A, and
MUL, MULHU, and all other operations clear both. Capture these bits with
their instruction in the existing ID/EX register; reset and flush clear
them, and a hold preserves them. Keep the original five-bit alu_op and
every ALU operation constant unchanged.

In the real-arithmetic ALU, form explicitly signed 33-bit operands
mul_a = $signed({mul_signed_a & a[31], a}) and
mul_b = $signed({mul_signed_b & b[31], b}). Compute one explicitly signed
66-bit mul_product = mul_a * mul_b. MUL selects mul_product[31:0]; the
grouped MULH/MULHU/MULHSU case selects mul_product[63:32]. The extension
preserves the complete unsigned range when the control is zero and the
signed RV32 value when it is one. Both slices therefore implement the
original RV32M results, including negative and maximum unsigned operands.
Product bits 65:64 are intentionally unused, not a reason to truncate an
input or the multiplication expression prematurely.

Remove the three separate product expressions. Feed the two registered
controls directly into the operand-extension bits; do not reconstruct
signedness from the binary opcode or divider/advance conditions in EX.
Select the single common high product for all three high-half operations
rather than rebuilding three masked copies of it. The intended effect is
simpler control around the already shared multiplier and fewer distinct
ALU result candidates. Do not add a multiplier pipeline, acceptance state,
busy signal, multiply-use bubble, output register, or operand isolation.

This is one multiply-control micro-optimization. Keep the existing ALU
interface's binary operation input for other arithmetic and the divider,
adding only the two signedness inputs. Preserve the four distinct original
multiplication ALTOPS formulas and constants under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS;
only the real branch combines their high-product selection. Preserve
forwarded operands, PC/link results, predictor, register-file paths,
pipeline advancement and holds, divider metadata and five-clock response,
bus handshakes, trap rules, strict raw-source RVFI values, and nret=1.

Estimate a three percent fitness gain from Fmax alone, with low confidence.
Neither a DSP-count reduction nor shorter CoreMark execution is predicted.
The new mode nets may become timing-critical, or remapping may worsen the
retained register-file paths. Inspect the mapped multiplier and its input
controls to determine whether the intended simplification actually occurred;
compare all three routed seeds and their median against 196.16 MHz and
fitness 467.44. Report marker-bracketed cycles separately and use unrounded
iterations/cycle. Instruction timing should remain unchanged under identical
bus-ready sequences.

unchanged ALTOPS formal, and stalled cosim before the standard FPGA flow.
Exercise every ordered multiply-mode transition with operands containing
both sign bits, all forwarding sources, data-bus holds, load-use bubbles,
division waits, flushes, and reset. ALTOPS is a routing/control check, not
proof of the new real multiplication expression; validate real arithmetic
against independent signed/unsigned reference products and use the existing

title: Align register-file ports with synchronous block RAM and MEM completion
motivation:
The retained winner's reproduced routed paths end at ID/EX operand
registers: MEM/WB.rd through write-through in seed 1 and stored RF words
through the read muxes in seeds 2 and 3. Its median is 196.16 MHz and
fitness is 467.44. Structural history rules out simply changing storage
or moving another mux. The asynchronous distributed-RAM attempt r3s1
saved substantial area but lost 16.70 percent fitness; bank retiming
r5s1 and r7s1 exposed operand-selection or remaining WB bypass paths;
moving writes to MEM completion alone in r6s1 lost 10.68 percent.
These changes also repeatedly exposed the unchanged EX ALU-control
path. A synchronous-memory port architecture can remove the wide ID
read network without widening EX forwarding, but whole-core timing
remains an explicit risk. The installed Gowin memory mapping supports
synchronous simple-dual-port block RAM with separate read/write enables.

moving writes to MEM completion alone in r6s1 lost 10.68 percent.
These changes also repeatedly exposed the unchanged EX ALU-control
path. A synchronous-memory port architecture can remove the wide ID

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the flop register file and its separate ID/EX operand flops
with two coherent, inferred synchronous block-RAM replicas, one per
source port. Each replica stores all 32 architectural words and shares
the single write stream. Its clocked read output becomes the operand
register at the existing ID/EX boundary: sample the incoming decoded
source address on exactly the edge that accepts its instruction
metadata, and deliver the corresponding word directly to EX afterward.
Remove the additional ID-stage capture of that word. This adds no
instruction stage, dependency bubble, or memory-bus cycle.

The essential accompanying port retiming is to write both RAM replicas
on the MEM completion edge, when that instruction enters MEM/WB.
Generate the write enable from the valid, advancing MEM instruction,
its final trap-corrected reg_write, nonzero rd, and !reset. A stalled
memory request or an alignment/illegal trap cannot write. Select the
same final ALU-or-extended-load value that the existing WB path will
expose after the edge. Keep architectural retirement and RVFI order
at MEM/WB; the earlier internal RF update creates no extra retirement.
The WB stage continues supplying the existing forwarding and RVFI data.

This timing makes a simultaneous accepted RF read and MEM write use
an existing producer age. After that edge, the just-written producer
is in MEM/WB, so ordinary MEM/WB-to-EX forwarding supplies its value.
A producer already in WB before the edge wrote the RAM one clock
earlier, so its value is available from storage without a saved WB
snapshot. Retain the current three EX candidates and priority:
EX/MEM, retained MEM/WB, then the synchronous RF word. Keep the existing
full source-tag comparisons and trap-corrected producer eligibility.
Do not add a fourth forwarding source, a serial write-through data
mux, or a new hazard stall. Together, synchronous reads and MEM-edge
writes form one structural change to the register-file port timing.

Avoid relying on device-specific cross-port read/write collision data.
Compare each incoming read address with the actual enabled MEM write
address. On a matching nonzero address, suppress that port's RAM read
clock enable and capture a false stored-word-use bit; its raw operand
output is consequently zero. The normal MEM/WB bypass, or a newer
eligible EX/MEM writer, must supply the architectural operand. Do not
suppress the write. This eliminates the physical collision without
synthesis-only don't-care assumptions, unmodeled primitives, or a
formal-only storage implementation. Inspect mapping for any unwanted
collision-emulation mux or external read register that would undo
the intended structure.

Leave RAM data arrays unreset and use a shared, synchronously reset
written-valid bitmap for x1 through x31. A real MEM write sets the
corresponding bit in both replicas' shared metadata; reset clears
all bits in one edge and suppresses writes. At read acceptance,
capture whether the source is nonzero, was previously written, and
did not collide. Mask the synchronous word to zero otherwise. A first
write colliding with a read is handled by the same WB forwarding rule.
This preserves all-registers-zero behavior after cold or warm reset
without resetting RAM contents, an initialization sweep, or dependence
on power-up values. Use portable inferred RTL with a block-RAM style
attribute supported by the existing flow; do not change synthesis files.

Both read-output state and its stored-word-use metadata must follow
the same acceptance, hold, reset, and flush decisions as ID/EX.
A flush clears operand usability and instruction metadata even when
the ordinary read enable is low. During a dmem hold, keep the read
outputs and ID/EX stable; existing retained MEM/WB data must remain
forwarding-eligible after its retirement valid clears. Division still
snapshots fully resolved operands and RVFI originals exactly once at
acceptance, before older producers drain, and finishes from div_meta_q.
A newly accepted successor gets a new synchronous read on the divider
completion edge. All ALU, branch, JALR, store-data, and RVFI consumers
must use the same final forwarded operands.

The estimated gain is five percent from Fmax with identical instruction
latencies and identical marker-bracketed cycles under matched stall
traces. Confidence is low because block-RAM placement and clock-to-data
delay, MEM write-data setup, read-enable qualification, valid masking,
or the unchanged EX ALU can become critical. At unchanged workload
cycles, break-even is 196.16 MHz and five percent requires 205.97 MHz.
Verify that the two logical replicas actually map into Gowin block
RAM with clocked reads and that the large flop-array read network is
gone; area savings or a local timing improvement alone do not validate
the hypothesis. Compare all three routed critical paths, RAM/LUT4/FF
use, exact cycles, median Fmax, and fitness against the retained winner.

Run the existing lint, complete cocotb, single-channel formal, stalled
ISS cosim, and three-seed FPGA gates without modifying their contracts.
Require identical architectural traces and cycle timing under matched
bus schedules, including x0, traps, long holds, and reset. Preserve
nret=1, every external port, decoder legality, arithmetic and ALTOPS,
predictor behavior, one-time stores, forward progress, and contiguous
single-channel retirement. Use the evaluator's identical workload and
exact iterations/cycle rather than its rounded IPC field. Prior logs
distinguish the checked-in scored workload from separate 6 KB runs;
change neither the benchmark nor its evaluator, and also require the
specified 6 KB CRCs d4b0/be52/5e47, valid start/stop markers, bounded
addresses, and the exact Correct operation validated. UART literal.

implementation_notes:
# Synchronous RF ports and MEM-completion writes

Implemented the structural hypothesis. Correctness and cycle equivalence passed, but the performance hypothesis failed: median routed Fmax fell from 196.16 to 141.88 MHz and fitness fell from 467.44 to 338.09 (27.67%). The two inferred block-RAM replicas are present and the flop-array operand read network is gone. All three new critical paths instead traverse the unchanged EX ALU-control/result-selection logic. This candidate should not replace the retained winner on fitness.

## Implementation

- `reg_file.sv` now contains two coherent, unreset 32 x 32 arrays with `ram_style = "block"`. Each has a clocked read output and an independent read enable; both receive the same physical write tuple. The two read enables are connected to `!stall_id` in the core.
- An enabled nonzero MEM write colliding with an incoming source suppresses only that port's RAM read enable. Its captured stored-word-use bit becomes false and its raw EX fallback is zero. No write-data bypass, saved WB snapshot, fourth forwarding source, new stall, or additional pipeline stage was added.
- A shared synchronously reset written bitmap masks unwritten registers. Both usability bits reset or flush even when their ordinary read enables are low. RAM words and raw read registers have no reset. A dmem/divider hold preserves the RF read registers and usability with ID/EX.
- `id_ex_t` and `id_stage` retain source tags and all instruction/control/prediction metadata but no operand-data flops. The RF outputs feed the existing three-source EX muxes directly, with unchanged EX/MEM-over-retained-MEM/WB priority. Fully resolved operands continue to feed ALU, branch, JALR, stores and RVFI. Divider acceptance still snapshots `next_ex` once into `div_meta_q`; completion and successor acceptance retain their original timing.
- `mem_stage` exposes `rf_w_en`, `rf_w_addr`, and `rf_w_data`. The enable requires `in.valid`, final trap-corrected `reg_write`, no illegal/alignment trap, nonzero `rd`, `!hold_wb`, and `!reset`. Data is the same final extended-load/ALU choice exposed in WB after that edge. MEM/WB capture, retained forwarding payload, memory handshakes and retirement order are unchanged.
- WB still produces the forwarding/RVFI result. Its unused internal write-enable/address outputs were removed after moving the physical write to MEM. Every top-level core port and `nret: 1` remain unchanged.

Minor deviations: the bitmap is indexed `[31:0]`, with bit zero permanently clear, to avoid address subtraction from a `[31:1]` variable index. Synthesis retains only 31 written-state flops plus the two usability flops. Separate port enables permit independent RF unit testing, while the actual pipeline drives them identically. No decoder, arithmetic, ALTOPS, hazard or predictor behavior was changed.

## Local gates

- Exact requested Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings. `git diff --check`: PASS.
- Complete cocotb: all seven runners PASS, **108 active tests passed, zero failures**. One optional artifact-replay test is skipped without an external trace directory; it was also run explicitly against the retained RTL and passed.

title: Private Gray-coded agree counters with simpler local updates
motivation:
The retained r4s2 predictor improved fitness to 467.44 with 32 private
saturating agree counters. Subsequent table expansion, history indexing,
and shared hysteresis all regressed fitness. In particular, r7s2 saved
storage but introduced confidence interference and increased scored
cycles by 0.064%. Its result suggests simplifying each private counter
without changing confidence ownership or the prediction sequence.
A proposal-stage standalone Gowin synthesis of the recoding below reduced
LUT1-through-LUT4 cells from 161 to 148, retaining 64 counter flip-flops,
seven queued-event flip-flops, and five MUX2_LUT5 cells. This local result
supports a smaller update circuit; it does not establish whole-core area,
routed Fmax, or fitness improvement.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Recode each existing two-bit agree counter as two PRIVATE bits: P is the
agreement prediction and H is strong confidence. Keep counters[entry][1]
as P and use counters[entry][0] as H, preserving the array dimensions,
generated constant-index updates, and existing MSB-only lookup wiring.
Reset every entry to P=1,H=1, the same strongly-agree prediction as today.
The correspondence to the current arithmetic counter C is:
  C=0, strongly disagree: P=0,H=1
  C=1, weakly disagree:   P=0,H=0
  C=2, weakly agree:      P=1,H=0
  C=3, strongly agree:   P=1,H=1
Adjacent saturating states differ in one bit. On a matching queued event
with actual agreement A, compute both assignments from PRE-EDGE state:
  P_next = H ? P : A
  H_next = (P == A)
These equations implement exactly the original two-bit saturating
predictor, including both endpoints and both weak-state reversals.
Use nonblocking assignments in the existing per-entry sequential block.
Remove the arithmetic increment/decrement and explicit endpoint tests.
Every entry retains its own H; training one entry cannot change another
entry's prediction or confidence. There is no selected-counter feedback
mux, additional lookup input, or confidence logic in the fetch read cone.

Preserve the seven-bit registered training queue and its exact schedule:
capture EX validity/index/agreement every clock, drain the previous valid
event once regardless of new capture validity, and cancel it on reset.
A lookup accepted on an update edge must still sample the old P bit.
Keep the fixed PC hash, EX training qualification, accepted pred_taken,
direct-target calculation, and pipeline control intact. This hypothesis
requires only predictor-internal recoding and its test representation
adapter; it does not change any top-level ports or nret=1.

The benefit sought is lower predictor update cost while preserving its
exact predictions and cycle counts, including under stalls and recovery.
Verify equivalence by decoding P/H back to the ordinary 0..3 counter and
comparing against an independent arithmetic saturation model. Establish
all eight state/outcome transitions, reset, disabled updates, and queued
event timing. Existing IF and pipeline learning curves must remain exact;
no changed prediction expectations are justified by this recoding.

Estimate a 1% fitness improvement with low confidence. Prior failures
show that even local area reductions can worsen placement of unchanged
EX or register-file paths. Run the unchanged correctness gates and compare
bracketed CoreMark cycles and three-seed median routed Fmax separately;
compute fitness using unrounded iterations/cycle. Equal cycles are an
equivalence requirement for identical workloads and stall streams, not
evidence of a frequency gain. Preserve every legality, trap, liveness,
RVFI, memory-bound, CRC, timing-marker, and completion check. Prior logs
distinguish the unchanged scored ELF from supplemental 6 KB validation;
compare identical ELFs and configurations without changing the evaluator,
and retain the requested 6 KB CRC validation separately if needed.

title: Isolate binary ALU decoding behind registered result enables
motivation:
The experiment log repeatedly identifies ID/EX alu_op-to-EX/MEM result
paths after changes elsewhere in the core. In r8s0, simplifying the
already-shared multiplier left those paths critical in all three seeds
and reduced median Fmax from 196.16 to 142.61 MHz at unchanged cycles.
Register-file rewrites similarly exposed this ALU control bottleneck.

The earlier r1s0 full one-hot conversion increased its own baseline's
Fmax from 127.03 to 139.53 MHz, but added 404 LUT4 and left the MULHU
enable critical. That experiment preceded the retained sequential
divider. Revisit control predecode specifically for the current split
between combinational results and a registered division response, also
removing binary divide recognition from EX advancement control. The
retained r4s2 winner's reported worst paths end in ID/EX operand capture;
an EX timing improvement is therefore a hypothesis, not a measured
bottleneck in the retained winner or a guarantee of higher whole-core Fmax.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 16-bit alu_result_sel field to id_ex_t only. Bits 0 through 14
correspond to the unchanged ALU_ADD through ALU_MULHSU constants. Bit 15
selects the existing sequential divider response and denotes any of
ALU_DIV, ALU_DIVU, ALU_REM or ALU_REMU. Generate this mutually exclusive
vector from the decoder's existing dec_alu_op before the ID/EX register:
one matching bit for operations 0 through 14, bit 15 for operations 15
through 18, and zero for unsupported operation values. Keep decoder
legality authoritative and independent. Reset and flush clear the whole
field, and stalls retain it with the instruction. Preserve ctrl_t.alu_op
and its numeric encodings for the divider; do not widen downstream bundles.

Give alu.sv the registered result_sel input. Compute the existing
combinational arithmetic results using exactly the existing expressions,
and mask each result directly with its registered enable. Combine the
16 masked words with a balanced reduction, expressed as four groups of
four followed by a final OR. The division leaf is the existing div_result;
all four division operations share that one leaf because their operation
was captured by the sequential divider. An all-zero selector produces
zero. Do not explicitly reconstruct a binary selector, add priority
selection, or gate the normal result leaves with opcode comparisons.
Keep the binary op input connected only to the unchanged divider instance.

In ex_stage.sv, derive is_div from in.valid, !in.ctrl.is_illegal and the
registered bit 15 instead of comparing the five-bit opcode against four
division constants. Keep all subsequent request, busy, valid, consume,
stall and reset qualifications unchanged. This is part of the same
control-predecode change: leaving binary divide recognition on div_wait
would retain an opcode path into the EX/MEM advance/bubble selection.
Continue consuming the registered result through the existing direct
div_consume path and capturing fully forwarded division metadata once.

This changes control encoding at an existing stage boundary, with no
added execution stage or instruction latency. Preserve operand forwarding,
register-file reads and write-through, jump/link selection, branch
prediction, memory handshakes, trap behavior, raw-source RVFI values,
nret=1, and retirement order. Preserve all three real product expressions
and their widths and signedness; multiplier sharing remains the synthesis
tool's existing task. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, select the four original
multiply substitute formulas with their respective enables. The divider's
real and ALTOPS arithmetic, five-clock response latency, and held-response
protocol remain unchanged. No DSP-count or CoreMark cycle reduction is
predicted.

Estimate five percent higher fitness from Fmax alone, with low confidence.
Extra enable routing, synthesis sharing, or the existing ID operand path
can erase the benefit. Unlike r1s0, this proposal retains binary operation
identity exclusively for the sequential divider, registers its EX class
recognition, and uses one response leaf for all four divide operations.
Inspect the synthesized result/advance cones to confirm that binary
alu_op decoding no longer controls normal EX result selection or is_div;
report multiplier resource use and all three routed critical paths.

Run the unchanged lint, real-arithmetic cocotb, ALTOPS formal and stalled
cosim gates. Preserve every existing arithmetic and protocol assertion.
Compare the standard three-seed median Fmax and marker-bracketed fitness
against 196.16 MHz and 467.44, using unrounded iterations/cycle. With the
same workload and bus-ready sequence, bracketed cycles should remain
identical. Preserve the evaluator's workload and separately satisfy the
requested 6 KB canonical CRC, completion-text, marker and memory-bounds
checks. Modify no evaluation-contract file, other core or core.yaml.

title: Insert a fully registered fetch queue before decode
motivation:
The retained r4s2 core achieves 467.44 iterations/s with 196.16 MHz
median routed Fmax and 4,196,463 scored marker-bracketed cycles. Its
combinational IF/ID interface couples instruction delivery to decode:
backend holds waste ready fetch opportunities, and imem stalls directly
suppress decode. A real register boundary can separate these operations.

LESSONS.md and the structural history identify a specific failed design
to improve upon. The r4s1 two-entry FALL-THROUGH queue reduced scored
cycles by 4.76%, but median Fmax fell from 181.36 to 138.85 MHz. All three
routed worst paths went from the instruction-ready LFSR through the
offered-instruction/register-read network into ID/EX rs2_val. Removing
that live/head bypass by registering every fetched instruction addresses
the observed failure mechanism. This is a pipeline-boundary experiment,
rather than another change to register-file storage or predictor policy.
Later structural RF changes also exposed unchanged EX control paths, so
shortening this particular cone alone does not establish a fitness gain.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a mandatory registered IF/ID boundary implemented as exactly two
fixed instruction entries, head and tail. Decode ALWAYS reads head's
registered PC, instruction and saved pred_taken. There is no empty-queue
fall-through, live-bus/head data mux, or combinational imemReady masking
of decode's instruction. The raw instruction bus and predictor output
terminate at frontend state. This single structural change combines
timing isolation with overlap of fetch and backend stalls. Retain the
existing RF, EX forwarding, ALU/divider, MEM/WB and nret=1 retirement.

Store the full 32-bit PC, 32-bit instruction and prediction bit in each
entry, with registered occupancy or equivalent valid bits. Offer validity
depends only on registered occupancy; head data remains stable until a
pop, reset or recovery. Stale data in an invalid head is harmless only
because decode explicitly inserts an entirely inert ID/EX bubble and
hazard detection is qualified by head validity. Never capture RF operand
values at fetch: read the existing write-first RF when the head issues.

Define issue_fire/pop as a valid head actually entering ID/EX, excluding
reset, qualified recovery, load-use interlock, dmem hold and divider wait.
Define fetch_fire as io_imemReady AND available capacity (occupancy < 2
OR simultaneous pop), also excluding reset and recovery. Every accepted
fetch is stored and advances the fetch PC exactly once. An empty queue
can enqueue but cannot issue the new word on that edge. With one entry
and pop plus push, replace head with the accepted tuple. With two entries
and pop plus push, move old tail to head and capture the new tail. Cover
enqueue-only and pop-only transitions explicitly; occupancy remains 0..2.
This gives one instruction per clock after initial filling, including
simultaneous dequeue/enqueue at full capacity, without a live bypass.

Separate frontend capacity from backend issue readiness. Fetch may fill
either free entry during load-use, dmem or divider holds, and decode may
issue buffered instructions while imemReady is low. Detect the existing
conservative load-use hazard against the VALID registered head's source
fields, never the unrelated raw bus instruction. Preserve the one-cycle
load-use bubble and existing higher-priority dmem/divider holds. When
ID/EX may advance but the queue is empty, capture zero valid and zero
side-effect controls. EX/MEM and MEM/WB retain their existing drain,
retained forwarding payload, and exactly-once retirement semantics.
Derive offered validity independently of consumer readiness; capacity
may use pop, but pop must not depend on current fetch availability.

Preserve the current 32-entry agree predictor, PC hash, private binary
counters, registered EX training event, and raw B/J target arithmetic.
Lookup is for the fetch PC; sample pred_taken together with that fetch
at fetch_fire, and update PC along that prediction on the same edge.
Once queued, its prediction is immutable even if counters subsequently
train. EX still resolves and trains each advancing legal, nontrapping
conditional branch exactly once. An update-edge enqueue samples the old
counter MSB. Queuing changes lookup-to-resolution distance, so identical
CoreMark prediction counts and old pipeline learning curves are not
assumed; the predictor state-transition and event-accounting rules are
unchanged and must still be checked independently.

A qualified EX recovery takes priority over queue capacity and imemReady:
reject the same-cycle old-path fetch, invalidate both entries, flush the
younger ID issue and install the actual recovery PC atomically. Correct
predictions preserve queued successors. Keep EX recovery suppressed
while it is held by dmem/division; queued predictor-training events from
already-advanced branches must still drain normally. Reset cancels all
queue state and retains the existing divider/predictor reset behavior.
No killed instruction may start a divide, access dmem, write a register
or retire. All target calculations remain full-width and alignment traps
retain their current architectural behavior.

As required for prefetched instructions, flush younger bytes on an
advancing legal FENCE.I after older memory work can complete. Extend
frontend recovery to its PC+4 for the already-accepted MISC-MEM funct3=001
class, suppressing old-path enqueue on that edge. Do not change decoder
legality, ordinary FENCE behavior or FENCE.I's NOP architectural effects
and RVFI pc_next. This is instruction-queue invalidation, not a cache.

The deliberate cost is one extra fetch-to-decode clock, including one
additional refill clock on zero-wait misprediction recovery. Useful
prefetch overlap can reduce other bubbles, but earlier predictor samples
can delay learning and the queue cannot create instruction-bus bandwidth.
The retained core's RF-data/WB-to-ID paths and EX ALU selection may still
dominate routing after the bus-to-decode data path is cut. Estimate a 5%
fitness gain with LOW confidence; no cycle or timing gain is measured at
proposal time. Do not add unrelated RF, ALU or predictor changes to rescue
the experiment if this boundary fails to improve fitness.

Check the synthesized data cones to establish that raw imemData and
imemReady cannot reach ID/EX operand-data inputs without passing through
the registered head. Then run all unchanged lint, cocotb, formal, stalled
cosim and three-seed FPGA gates. Compare cycles and median routed Fmax
separately against r4s2 using identical ELFs/configurations. A gain needs
Fmax_new / 196.16 > cycles_new / 4196463 on the recorded scored workload;
use exact iterations/cycle, not the rounded core.yaml or log IPC value.
Inspect all three worst paths and whole-core LUT4/FF use. Prior records
distinguish the evaluator's scored 2 KB ELF from supplemental 6 KB
validation: keep the evaluator unchanged and retain the requested 6 KB
CRC checks d4b0/be52/5e47 separately. Preserve every legality, liveness,
arithmetic, memory-bound, RVFI-order, timing-marker and UART-completion
check, all top-level ports, and core.yaml nret=1.

implementation_notes:
Implemented the mandatory registered two-entry fetch queue. Correctness gates pass, but this experiment does not improve fitness: the scored workload uses 3.19% fewer cycles while median routed Fmax falls 17.16%, giving a 14.43% fitness regression. The implementation is retained for evaluation without unrelated RF, ALU, divider, or predictor changes.

Actual changes:

- `cores/bench/rtl/if_stage.sv` owns exactly two fixed entries, each containing a full 32-bit PC, 32-bit instruction, and saved prediction. A two-bit occupancy register supplies offered validity. Decode data comes directly from head registers, without an empty bypass or live readiness mask. Explicit enqueue-only, pop-only, and simultaneous transitions support full-capacity replacement. Reset clears all queue state; qualified recovery invalidates both entries, rejects the old-path enqueue, and installs the recovery PC.
- `core.sv` returns actual ID/EX acceptance as `issue_fire`. Fetch capacity is independent of load-use, dmem, and divider holds. `hazard_unit.sv` matches the conservative source fields of the valid registered head and preserves dmem/divider hold priority and the one-cycle load-use bubble. `id_stage.sv` reads the unchanged write-first RF when the head issues and captures an entirely zero bundle on an advancing empty input. Backend holds preserve the complete ID/EX payload.
- `ex_stage.sv` adds recovery to PC+4 for advancing legal MISC-MEM funct3=001 instructions. FENCE.I preserves its existing NOP controls, legality class, and RVFI next PC. title: Four-entry learned loop-exit override for the agree predictor
motivation:
The retained r4s2 agree predictor already handles stable branch bias well.
Increasing capacity in r5s2 saved only 0.14% of scored cycles, resolved
global history in r6s2 increased cycles, and both shared hysteresis and
private Gray recoding lost fitness. These results favor targeting a
remaining predictable event: the exit of a repeatedly executed fixed-trip
loop, which a strongly taken counter normally misses once per invocation.

A proposal-stage trace from the retained simulator, whose archived RTL
matches the current bench RTL, contains 529588 conditional branches inside
the scored timing markers. Two frequently executed backward branches each
exit 3240 times, always after eight taken outcomes. A retirement-order
software model of the specific four-entry design below reduces direction
errors from 47235 to 39276, with 7959 exit overrides and no incorrect
overrides on that trace. The model omits fetch timing and queued training;
these are direction-model results, not measured candidate cycles or Fmax.
The trip counts and branch identities must be learned at runtime.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one small loop-exit side predictor while retaining the current 32-entry
binary agree predictor and its training unchanged. The side predictor
overrides a conditional direction only to NOT TAKEN at a confidently
learned loop exit. It never supplies a target or forces a taken prediction.
All other predictions use the existing agree direction, and JAL/JALR
behavior remains unchanged.

Use four direct-mapped entries. Derive the two-bit index as
PC[3:2] XOR PC[8:7] and the twelve-bit tag as PC[15:4]. Each entry holds
valid, tag, a six-bit count of resolved taken outcomes since its last
not-taken outcome, a six-bit learned taken-run length, a two-bit confidence
counter, an overflow flag, and a registered exit_due bit. These partial
tags intentionally allow aliases above bit 15; aliases may affect accuracy
but can never bypass normal EX verification. Reset invalidates all entries
and clears their state. Do not initialize entries from benchmark addresses,
instruction sequences, marker activity, or known trip counts.

Train only backward conditional branches: reuse the existing EX
branch_train_valid qualification and additionally require in.instr[31].
Supply in.pc[15:2] and the fully forwarded branch_cond. Register the
sixteen-bit event {valid,index,tag,taken}, then apply the previously queued
event to one locally updated entry. Capture event validity every clock,
drain pending events despite later holds or recovery, and cancel pending
events on reset, exactly as the existing agree-training queue does.
There is no combinational EX-outcome or pending-event bypass to fetch.

On an invalid entry or tag mismatch, allocate that event's tag, clear
confidence, learned length, overflow, and exit_due, and set the current
count to one for a taken event or zero for a not-taken event. On a matching
taken event, increment the current count without wrapping. A taken event
when the pre-event count is 63 sets overflow and clears confidence; retain
that overflow until the next not-taken event. A taken event when exit_due
was set disproves the learned exit: immediately clear confidence and
exit_due while continuing to count the actual run.

On a matching not-taken event with a nonzero, nonoverflowed count, compare
the observed count with the learned length. If equal, saturating-increment
confidence; otherwise replace the learned length and set confidence to
one. A zero-length or overflowed run clears confidence and learned length.
Every not-taken event resets the current count and overflow. Thus three
matching completed nonzero runs establish confidence=3. A different run
length must establish confidence again. These rules also handle partial
first observations, changing trip counts, and taken runs longer than 63.

Register exit_due from each entry's post-update state: confidence=3,
nonzero learned length, no overflow, and current_count=learned_length.
Clear it on reset, replacement, invalid runs, and contrary outcomes.
Keep count arithmetic and count/length comparisons off the fetch cone.
Lookup combines the selected index, matching tag, valid, and exit_due;
only this one-bit exit override joins the existing branch direction.
Use constant-index local updates and a small parallel hit reduction,
avoiding a dynamically selected wide tag/count feedback datapath.

In IF, apply the override only to a legal backward conditional branch,
then retain the existing PC and immediate alignment checks, shared B/J
target adder, and accepted-fetch pred_taken bit. Predictions sample old
registered state on a training edge. Short or back-to-back loops can see
stale counts because training is delayed; they must simply recover through
the existing EX mismatch mechanism. Do not add speculative iteration
counters, checkpoints, a training bypass, or new pipeline stages to hide
that delay. EX remains authoritative for actual direction, alignment,
recovery target, traps, link values, and RVFI pc_next. Holds must preserve
the accepted prediction, and wrong-path fetches must not train either table.

The nominal additional state is 116 entry bits and 16 queued-event bits.
The intended benefit is fewer loop-exit recoveries, not a larger general
direction table. The +1% fitness estimate has low confidence: 7959 fewer
modeled direction errors amount to only about 0.19% of retained scored
cycles if each saves one cycle. Actual stalled cycles must be measured,
and even a small routed-frequency loss could erase the benefit. Prior
results do not justify assuming that predictor-local changes preserve
whole-core Fmax. Report cycles, LUT4/FF, and three-seed median Fmax
separately before calculating fitness from unrounded iterations/cycle.

Run the unchanged lint, unit, formal, cosim, and FPGA gates. Keep nret=1,
top-level ports, decoder legality, arithmetic, RVFI ordering, liveness,
memory bounds, timing markers, CRCs, and completion checks intact. The
profiling ELF is the unchanged scored workload with SHA-256
c2af1db144cd8fc7936f33f0a0e05a244938ebfc64c5fd362e5ffe88cde4a0d4.
Prior logs identify it as 2 KB; preserve that comparison and the evaluator,
and separately retain the requested 6 KB validation with canonical CRCs.

implementation_notes:
Implemented the four-entry learned loop-exit override. All correctness
gates pass, but measured fitness regresses 28.3158%: the 0.2032% cycle
reduction does not compensate for the routed-frequency loss.

`cores/bench/rtl/loop_predictor.sv` implements the specified runtime-only
index PC[3:2] XOR PC[8:7], partial tag PC[15:4], six-bit saturating taken
count, learned length, two-bit confidence, sticky overflow, and registered
exit_due. Replacement, zero-length runs, contrary taken outcomes, overflow,
and reset follow the proposed rules. The sixteen-bit event queue captures
validity every clock and applies its previous event exactly once, without
a training bypass. Four generated constant-index updates feed a parallel
hit reduction. There are no targets or speculative iteration counters.

IF instantiates the new predictor beside the unchanged 32-entry binary
agree predictor. Only a legal backward conditional can suppress the agree
direction. EX exports the existing branch training qualification AND
instruction bit 31, PC[15:2], and the fully forwarded branch condition.
Core wires those signals. Alignment checks, the shared B/J target adder,
accepted prediction metadata, EX resolution and recovery, pipeline bundles,
division, top-level ports, nret=1, and RVFI are unchanged.

The independent event-driven Python model uses unbounded resolved run
counts and derives expected overflow, saturation, and exit eligibility
without reading DUT exit_due. It checks every entry field and pending
event, old-state lookup, all four indices, tag replacement and high-address
aliases, confidence acquisition/saturation, early and late exits, lengths
0/1/63, overflow, random events, draining, and reset cancellation. IF tests
cover confident/unconfident lookup, forward and reserved encodings,
alignment, JAL/JALR, holds, recovery, and both assertion and clearing of
exit_due on a fetch acceptance edge.

The existing pipeline ISS/RVFI, agree-counter, order, PC chaining, trap,
memory transaction, and forwarding assertions remain active. Its new loop
scoreboard compares training with exactly-once legal backward EX advances
and matching retirements. Added programs demonstrate warmed exit recovery
removal, changing lengths, overflow and relearning, four resident tags plus
a fifth replacement, partial-tag aliases, consecutive backward branches,
wrong-path branches/stores, divider queue draining, memory holds,
load-to-branch forwarding, imem stalls on recovery, and reset with learned
state and pending training. Nine eight-taken invocations have exit gaps
of [2,2,2,1,1,1,1,1,1] retirement cycles. A two-instruction version retains
all exit misses despite confidence=3, explicitly checking the required
stale-count behavior and absence of a bypass.

No architectural deviations. A pending EX-branch event cannot coincide
with an actual MEM-stage dmem hold in this pipeline: that MEM instruction
is the branch itself. Tests exercise queued draining under IF holds and
divider holds, and accepted branch prediction stability during real dmem
holds, without injecting impossible EX events.

title: Registered ALU result selection with one explicitly shared multiplier
motivation:
The retained core scores 467.44 at 196.16 MHz. Experiment r9s0 removed
binary ALU decoding from the execution result and advancement cones,
but its independent one-hot multiply enables prevented Yosys SHARE from
proving exclusivity: MULT36X36 use increased from one to three and median
Fmax fell to 176.34 MHz. Experiment r8s0 demonstrated a single explicitly
shared signed 33x33 multiplier with registered operand signedness, but
its unchanged binary ALU result selection remained timing-critical and
median Fmax fell to 142.61 MHz. Neither experiment reduced CoreMark cycles.
A coherent predecoded ALU implementation can address both documented
implementation problems together: directly registered result controls
feeding a single multiplication datapath whose sharing is structural.

Replace the EX binary result-selection network with a registered,

# Registered ALU selection and one shared multiplier

Implemented the hypothesis, with all local correctness gates passing. **The
performance criterion failed:** median routed Fmax is 175.56 MHz and fitness is
418.35231241166667 (reported as 418.35), below the retained 467.44. This candidate
should not replace the retained core on fitness. No further microarchitectural
change was made to chase the result.

## Implementation

- Added `alu_result_sel[13:0]`, `mul_signed_a`, and `mul_signed_b` only to
  `id_ex_t`. Bits 0–10 retain ADD–LUI numbering, 11 selects MUL low, 12 selects
  the common high product, and 13 selects the divider response.
- ID decodes the existing binary operation with an explicit zero default.
  The new fields share the existing complete-bundle reset/flush priority,
  acceptance enable, and stall hold.
- EX passes these registered controls directly to the ALU and qualifies the
  divide-group bit with the original validity and legality checks.
- Real multiplication is one signed 33-by-33 product into 66 bits. Operand sign
  extensions use the registered modes; results use bits 31:0 and 63:32.
  Fourteen individually masked result leaves feed a balanced four-level OR
  tree padded with two zero leaves. There is no priority selection or opcode
  re-encoding, and no added product register, isolation mux, handshake, or stall.
- Preserved the original ALTOPS MUL constant/formula. The shared high leaf uses
  modes 11/10/00 for the original MULH/MULHSU/MULHU formulas and constants.
- `divider.sv`, `core.sv`, `ctrl_t`, all binary operation constants, decoder
  legality, forwarding, RVFI source values, jump links, prediction/training,
  retirement, and memory behavior are unchanged. `nret` remains 1.

Only four RTL files and the two requested local test files changed, plus this
explicitly requested writeup. No other core or evaluation-contract file changed.

## Correctness and latency

- Requested Verilator lint command: **PASS**, no warnings. ALTOPS lint also
  passed without warnings.
- Unchanged `make test TARGET=bench`: **PASS**, all 7 runners and all 109 cocotb
  cases; no skipped cases. This includes 31 ALU and 31 pipeline cases.
- Added independent Python products for signed extrema, both operand orders,
  random values, and every ordered transition among all four multiply modes.
  Added zero selection, integer/multiply/divider transitions, held divider
  responses, and every binary opcode value with fixed normal result controls.
- Pipeline checks compare the held command against an instruction-derived
  oracle and check acceptance, full-bundle hold/clear, both forwarding sources,
  load-use bubbles, memory stalls, divider acceptance/response, redirects,
  illegal encodings, and reset. Directed dependent multiply chains cover all
  16 ordered mode transitions. Ordinary instructions retire one cycle apart.
  Existing ISS/RVFI comparison, raw sources, memory transaction counts,
  exact-once retirement, contiguous order, and predictor assertions remain.
- Unchanged `bash formal/run_all.sh`, automatically selecting the nret=1 wrapper
  and ALTOPS config: **PASS, 53 passed / 0 failed**. No counterexample and no RTL
  fix attempts. The initial launch stopped before generating checks because
  the default Python lacked PyYAML; selecting the already-installed Python
  environment resolved this without modifying the script or formal config.
- Unchanged standard cosim gate: **PASS**, selftest and scored CoreMark ELF.
  Additional selftest runs with `--istall --dstall --seed 1/2/3` each matched all
  115 retirements using the unchanged ISS and RVFI comparator.
- Real arithmetic was exercised by cocotb and cosim. `formal-deep` was not run;
  the formal result above is explicitly the required ALTOPS gate.

## Workload and cycle comparison

Built the retained pre-edit RTL and candidate separately. Each pair ran the
same byte-identical ELF with the unchanged simulator's default deterministic
bus-ready stream and `--bench --istall --dstall`. Both marker endpoints, the
bracketed cycle count, and the complete UART output match exactly.

| Workload | Start marker | Stop marker | Retained cycles | Candidate cycles |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Scored 2 KB, 10 iterations, -O3 | 14,996 | 4,211,459 | 4,196,463 | 4,196,463 |
| Separate 6 KB, 10 iterations, -O3 | 52,759 | 30,783,321 | 30,730,562 | 30,730,562 |

The unchanged evaluator and build rules score 2 KB. That contract was preserved.
The 6 KB ELF was built separately outside the scored workload location. Its
`crclist=d4b0`, `crcmatrix=be52`, `crcstate=5e47`, `seedcrc=8a02`, and
`crcfinal=5949` all match. Both workloads completed with EBREAK, `oob=false`,
positive marker brackets, 10 iterations, and the literal
`Correct operation validated.`. The UART's pre-existing compiler-description
string says `-O2`; the actual compiler invocations for both ELFs used `-O3`.

ELF SHA-256:

- Scored 2 KB: `a3b3906aeba4fa63950e6863838ab8328da3b1f509588769ae2b9f63bf8718e8`
- Separate 6 KB: `a7fa27a60b9e14531c6419293fcb3aa48e925b2b95c6d143539d624f90579c0a`

## Mapped implementation

The standard Yosys Gowin synthesis contains **exactly one `MULT36X36`**,
`cpu.u_ex.u_alu.mul_product_MULT36X36_DOUT`. Its clock, enable, and reset are
constant zero; this is a combinational multiplication datapath.

All fourteen result bits and both signedness bits are driven directly by
`DFFRE.Q` outputs. Every one has the same CE net 2813 and reset net 2815.
The result-select bits are ID/EX bits 36–49; signedness occupies bits 35/34.
Thus there is no post-register reconstruction of the command.

A forward traversal of the mapped binary opcode's combinational fanout stops
at exactly 64 divider capture D inputs: 31 quotient bits, 31 divisor bits,
`negate_q`, and `select_rem_q`. There are **no non-divider sequential
endpoints**, including normal EX result or advancement controls. The traversal
stops at sequential cells and does not mistake the captured division behavior
for a combinational path.

The standard whole-design nextpnr utilization, including the unchanged benchmark
wrapper, is **6,198 LUT4 / 2,293 FF / 1 MULT36X36 / 4 BSRAM**, identical across
all three seeds. The retained reported utilization is 6,146 LUT4 / 2,260 FF /
1 MULT36X36: this candidate adds 52 LUT4 and 33 FF. These are whole-design
counts, not the local ALU cone's resource count.

Ran unchanged `make fpga TARGET=bench` with `NRET=1` and the single-channel
benchmark wrapper selected. All three routes completed normally. The final

| 2 | 175.56 MHz | ID/EX `ctrl.is_jump` | EX/MEM `alu_result[1]` | 2.78 ns | 2.91 ns | 5.70 ns |
| 3 | 178.57 MHz | ID/EX `alu_result_sel[13]` | EX/MEM `alu_result[1]` | 3.15 ns | 2.45 ns | 5.60 ns |

Logic/routing subtotals and path totals above are independently rounded in the
nextpnr report. Exact reported cell endpoints and stage sequences:

- Seed 1: `cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_182.Q` to
  `cpu.u_ex.reg_q_DFFR_Q_62.D`.
  `DFFRE -> LUT4 -> LUT4 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> LUT4 -> LUT4 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> LUT4 -> DFFR`.
- Seed 2: `cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_153.Q` to

  `DFFRE -> LUT4 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> LUT4 -> LUT4 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> LUT4 -> DFFR`.
- Seed 3: `cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_182.Q` to

  `DFFRE -> LUT4 -> LUT4 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> LUT4 -> LUT4 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> MUX2_LUT5 -> LUT4 -> DFFR`.

Median Fmax is **175.56 MHz**, down 10.50% from 196.16 MHz. Fitness uses the
unrounded ratio `10 / 4196463 = 2.3829591729987848e-6` iterations/cycle:

This is a **10.50% regression** against 467.44 at identical cycles. The
structural sharing and predecode objectives succeeded, but the remaining

title: Register four ALU result lanes before their final merge
motivation:
The retained core scores 467.44 iterations/s at 196.16 MHz. The structural
multiplier, register-file and fetch-queue experiments repeatedly left
ID/EX ALU-control to EX/MEM result selection timing-critical. In r9s1,
even removing the raw instruction-bus path into decode and saving 3.19%
of scored cycles lost 14.43% fitness. This favors directly changing the
execute-result register boundary. The r9s0 result-enable experiment kept
the final ALU reduction before that boundary, lost 10.10% fitness, and
unintentionally expanded one shared multiplier into three. The proposed
experiment moves the final reduction across the boundary and explicitly
retains one product datapath. It does not assume DSP delay is the present
bottleneck or infer a timing improvement from a local logic-depth change.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the single selected EX/MEM ALU-result register with four parallel
32-bit result-lane registers at the SAME pipeline boundary. Each lane
computes a small, disjoint operation class and returns zero when inactive:
arithmetic for ADD/SUB/SLT/SLTU, logic for AND/OR/XOR/LUI, shifts for
SLL/SRL/SRA, and M-extension for MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU or a consumed
divider response. Perform operation selection and inactive-lane masking
locally before each lane register. After the registers, form the final
architectural ALU result with one four-input bitwise OR per result bit.
There must be no global four-lane merge on any EX/MEM result-lane D input,
and no opcode-controlled final mux after these registers. This is one
structural retiming of result selection, with unchanged instruction
stages, issue width, execution latencies and retirement boundary.

ADD-based effective addresses and AUIPC use the arithmetic lane. A valid
JAL/JALR link routes PC+4 through that lane and forces all other lanes
to zero. Preserve the existing branch/JALR target computations and trap
handling independently of this result representation. At most one lane
is active for an instruction; an active lane may itself contain zero.
Unsupported operations and inert bubbles produce four zero lanes.
Keep decoder legality and its default-illegal policy authoritative.

Avoid the multiplier replication observed in r9s0 by defining exactly
one real product expression inside the M lane. Sign-extend each operand
to 33 bits only when its operation requires signed interpretation:
both for MULH, only A for MULHSU, neither for MULHU or low-half MUL.
Multiply these explicitly signed 33-bit operands into a signed 66-bit
product; select bits 31:0 for MUL and 63:32 for the high variants. Keep
this selection inside the M lane, before its EX/MEM register. The
explicit product is necessary to preserve sharing while changing the
result topology, not a separate multiplier-pipelining experiment.
Preserve all four multiply ALTOPS formulas in this same lane. Leave
the divider arithmetic, ALTOPS implementation and five-clock response
protocol unchanged. Confirm the mapped product still uses one
MULT36X36; do not assume source-level sharing proves the mapping.

Merge the four registered lanes once for EX/MEM-to-EX forwarding and
the value captured into the existing MEM/WB.alu_result field. Retain
the current three operand-source ages and youngest-writer priority;
the forward unit receives one merged EX/MEM word, not four new sources.
For a memory instruction, its effective address comes directly from
the registered arithmetic lane. Use that address consistently for
dmem outputs, alignment checking, byte extraction, masks and RVFI.
Memory instructions cannot select another lane. Keep MEM/WB's existing
load-versus-ALU writeback representation and RF write-through behavior.
The existing load-use bubble remains, including its current source
comparison policy; no new dependency bypass or fetch/predictor change
belongs to this experiment.

All four registers advance, hold, reset and bubble atomically with the
EX/MEM instruction metadata. A data-memory stall preserves the entire
bundle. During divider work, let older work drain and insert completely
inert EX/MEM bubbles exactly as today. Capture fully forwarded original
operands and RVFI metadata at divide acceptance; clear saved result
lanes then. On the single permitted response-consumption edge, restore
that metadata and write div_result only into the M lane, clearing the
other three. A held response or a prior lane value must never leak into
another instruction, replay a store, or cause a second retirement.
Preserve retained MEM/WB forwarding data when its valid bit is cleared
by dmem backpressure. Reset cancels all outstanding state as before.

The intended benefit is a shorter local EX result-selection network,
with its final reduction moved to a shallow OR of registered values.
The deliberate cost is up to 96 additional EX/MEM data bits before
optimization and an OR on the EX/MEM forwarding and MEM capture paths.
That forwarding delay, extra routing, the remaining local operation
selectors or the unchanged RF path can erase the benefit. Estimate a
five-percent fitness gain with low confidence. This is unmeasured.
With identical ELF and bus-ready sequence, marker-bracketed cycles
should be unchanged; any difference requires explanation as a potential
protocol regression. Inspect all three routed critical paths, complete
LUT4/FF/DSP use, and the actual register-to-register cones to establish
whether the intended boundary moved and whether whole-core timing won.

Run the unchanged lint, cocotb, ALTOPS formal, stalled cosim and
three-seed FPGA evaluation. Retain every existing assertion and exact
arithmetic vector; independently test real multiplication, since
ALTOPS cannot validate the rewritten product expression. Attempt the
applicable real-arithmetic formal-deep checks when feasible and report
incomplete proofs accurately. Compare exact iterations/cycle and
median Fmax against the retained core using the same evaluator ELF and
configuration. For the recorded scored run, improvement requires
Fmax_new / 196.16 > cycles_new / 4196463. Keep the evaluator unchanged
and separately retain the requested canonical 6 KB CRC checks
d4b0/be52/5e47, both timing markers, bounds checks and the literal
Correct operation validated. Preserve nret=1, the exact core ports,
single in-order channel-0 retirement, contiguous RVFI order, legal and
misalignment trap behavior, liveness and all other hard invariants.

title: Bank agree counters by branch condition polarity
motivation:
The retained r4s2 core reaches 467.44 iterations/s with 32 private binary
agree counters, queued EX training, and 196.16 MHz median routed Fmax.
LESSONS.md and the predictor records in experiments/log.jsonl show that
doubling capacity saved only 0.14% of scored cycles, global-history
indexing increased cycles, and counter recoding and loop overrides lost
fitness. These results favor changing how the existing counters are
allocated while keeping their state, update logic, and training latency.

A retirement-order model using the retained branch-event trace contains
529588 conditional branches inside the scoring markers. The current
PC-only index produces 47235 modeled direction errors. Partitioning the
same 32 counters by branch funct3 bit zero, with the four-bit PC hash
specified below, produces 44854 errors: 2381 fewer, or approximately
5.04% fewer direction errors. The model trains on every trace event,
including warmup, and counts errors only inside the markers. It omits
fetch timing, queued training, and candidate-dependent bus-stall timing;
these numbers are not measured candidate cycles or Fmax.

The proposed split separates complementary branch-condition classes
without allocating additional counters or changing a branch's context
over time. Two parallel 16-entry reads also allow the late instruction
polarity bit to select only the final one-bit result.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Reallocate the existing 32 two-bit agree counters into two banks of
sixteen, selected by the conditional branch's funct3[0], instruction
bit 12. Bank zero contains BEQ, BLT, and BLTU; bank one contains BNE,
BGE, and BGEU. Use slot = PC[5:2] XOR PC[10:7] in both banks, and encode
the five-bit training index as {instruction[12], slot}. This is a fixed
runtime policy for every program, with no address-specific entries,
initialized outcomes, benchmark detection, or learned PC constants.

Retain exactly 32 private binary saturating counters, reset to 11, and
the existing seven-bit registered training event. Preserve the local
per-entry update blocks, saturation transitions, unconditional capture
of event validity, previous-event drain, and reset cancellation. Each
queued event updates exactly one counter using that entry's current
state. A later hold or recovery must not discard a pending event.

Change branch_predictor's lookup index to four bits and expose two
agreement MSBs, one from each bank. Read the two sixteen-bit MSB vectors
concurrently using the PC-derived slot. Keep instruction bits outside
both table-read cones. In IF, select the returned bank MSB with raw
imem_data[12], then retain the current bias conversion:
branch_direction = imem_data[31] XOR NOT selected_agree_msb.
The bank choice and bias conversion together have four logical inputs
and can fit one LUT4; verify the actual synthesis result. Do not turn
this into a serial instruction-dependent table lookup or read full
two-bit counters dynamically. No EX or queued-event bypass feeds fetch.

EX recomputes the same five-bit {polarity, slot} index from its held
instruction and PC. Agreement remains branch_cond == in.instr[31],
using fully forwarded operands. Train only a valid, legal, nontrapping
conditional branch advancing from EX, with the existing !reset, !stall,
and !div_wait qualifications, including advances that assert recovery.
Because both index components belong to the instruction, no history
checkpoint or additional prediction metadata is needed. Existing core
training wires remain five bits wide.

Preserve raw legal-branch predecode, word-alignment eligibility, JAL
prediction, JALR fallback, the shared B/J target adder, and the accepted
pred_taken bit. Fetch samples pre-edge counter state; predictions only
change PC when the instruction is accepted. Preserve prediction holds
and bubble clearing, EX direction-mismatch recovery, recovery priority
over imem stalls, and deferred recovery during dmem/divider holds. EX
remains authoritative for architectural next PC, traps, and RVFI.
New within-bank collisions affect prediction accuracy only.

Estimate a one-percent fitness improvement with low confidence. The
modeled 2381 fewer errors correspond to only about 0.057% of the retained
4196463 scored cycles if each removed one cycle. The estimate therefore
depends mainly on a modest routed-frequency gain from the parallel
sixteen-way reads and final bank/bias selection. Halving the capacity
available to each condition class can introduce interference, and
whole-core placement can erase local timing improvements, as the prior
experiments demonstrate. Report actual cycles, LUT4/FF, and three-seed
median Fmax separately, then compute fitness with unrounded iterations
per cycle. No candidate performance has been measured for this proposal.

Run the unchanged lint, cocotb, formal, stalled cosim, and FPGA gates.
Confirm the predictor still has 64 counter bits plus seven event bits,
and inspect the mapped lookup cones and full-core critical paths. Keep
all architectural, legality, liveness, RVFI order, memory-bound, marker,
CRC, and completion checks intact, including the declared nret=1 ports.
Prior experiment notes identify the unchanged scored ELF as 2 KB with
SHA-256 c2af1db144cd8fc7936f33f0a0e05a244938ebfc64c5fd362e5ffe88cde4a0d4;
that is the workload behind the trace and 467.44 comparison. Preserve
the evaluator and compare identical workloads. Separately retain the
requested 6 KB, -O3, ten-iteration stalled validation with canonical
CRCs d4b0/be52/5e47; do not substitute its cycle count into that score.

title: Fold jump-link writeback into the existing binary ALU selector
motivation:
The retained core selects an ALU result and then applies a separate
ctrl.is_jump-controlled PC+4 override before EX/MEM. Every ordinary ALU
result passes through that additional selection. The r10s0 micro_opt
experiment removed binary EX result decoding but still regressed to
175.56 MHz; its median routed critical path started at ID/EX ctrl.is_jump
and ended at EX/MEM alu_result[1]. That is evidence from a related
implementation, not a measurement of the retained core's critical path,
but the same final jump override remains in the current RTL.

LESSONS.md and the micro_opt history also show that broad one-hot ALU
changes can disrupt multiplier sharing and placement. A smaller change
can absorb the jump-link result into the existing binary selector while
preserving its mutually exclusive multiply arms. This directly targets
serial result selection without adding result lanes or pipeline state.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Treat the JAL/JALR link value as one additional internal ALU operation.
Append ALU_LINK = 5'd19 to the existing constants, keeping operation
numbers 0 through 18 unchanged. Set this operation only inside the
decoder's already-validated JAL and funct3=0 JALR arms. The existing
ctrl_t.alu_op field and ID/EX register carry it with the instruction;
no extra selector flops, operation re-encoding, or new pipeline stage
are needed.

Add a 32-bit link_value input to alu.sv, driven in EX by the existing
full-width expression in.pc + 32'd4. Add ALU_LINK: out = link_value to
the same binary case that selects the current integer and M-extension
results. Make next_ex.alu_result take alu_result directly, removing
the subsequent in.ctrl.is_jump ? PC+4 : alu_result mux. Keep link_value
independent of forwarded operands and the normal alu_a/alu_b muxes.
Reuse the PC+4 expression for existing sequential-PC uses where the
synthesizer already shares it; do not introduce another adder or a
separate selector around the ALU output.

Keep ctrl.is_jump and ctrl.is_jalr for control-flow resolution, target
generation, alignment faults, redirects and architectural pc_next.
JALR must still use the fully forwarded rs1 plus its immediate for the
target, clear target bit zero, and trap a misaligned target with its
link write suppressed. JAL predictions, recovery, x0 writes and all
existing hold/flush/reset priorities remain unchanged. Preserve the
divider's separate div_consume result override, metadata capture,
five-clock response, and inert bubbles. Keep all multiply expressions,
signed widths, and every RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formula unchanged; the new
link operation selects the same PC+4 value in both build modes.

This is one result-mux micro-optimization. The intended gain is about
three percent in median routed Fmax at identical marker-bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Confidence is low because synthesis may already merge
parts of the two selectors, the additional case arm may increase opcode
fanout, or whole-core placement may dominate. Inspect the mapped cone
to establish whether the serial jump override was actually removed,
verify that one MULT36X36 is still inferred, and report all three routed
critical paths and LUT4/FF use. Do not infer success from RTL mux count.

Run the unchanged lint, cocotb, formal and stalled cosim gates, then the
standard three-seed FPGA evaluation. Use the same ELF and deterministic
bus-ready stream for the retained and candidate cores; instruction
timing and bracketed cycles should match. Compute fitness from exact
iterations/cycle and compare against 467.44. Preserve the evaluator's
existing workload; prior logs identify its scored ELF as 2 KB. Also
retain the requested separate 6 KB, -O3, ten-iteration validation with
CRCs d4b0/be52/5e47, both timing markers, completion text and bounds.
Preserve nret=1, all raw-source RVFI fields, retirement ordering, and
every legality check. Change no evaluation file or other core.

title: Decouple RAM-store completion with a single-entry write buffer
motivation:
The retained core freezes IF, ID and EX whenever a MEM-stage store sees
dmemReady low, although a store needs no returned data. A small buffer
can retain its complete transaction while younger arithmetic proceeds.
The structural history has already tested multiplier pipelining,
register-file storage and retiming, two fetch-queue organizations, and
registered ALU-result lanes. Those changes regressed routed fitness;
r4s1 and r9s1 saved cycles but added frontend timing costs, while r10s1
preserved cycles and lost 11.74 percent fitness. No logged structural
attempt decouples store completion from the external write handshake.
This offers cycle savings without changing instruction delivery or
adding another operand-forwarding source to the critical EX path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert exactly one write-buffer entry between MEM and the data bus.
It holds a full 32-bit byte address, the already replicated 32-bit
store data, four byte enables and a valid bit. A valid, legal, aligned
store to ordinary RAM may complete into MEM/WB once this transaction
has either been accepted by the bus or durably captured in the entry.
Completion releases the existing pipeline hold; external acceptance
may follow later. This is one structural change to memory-stage
completion and bus ownership. Keep the scalar pipeline, arithmetic,
RF, predictor, load-use policy and nret=1 retirement boundary.

Use empty-buffer fall-through so zero-wait stores still use the
current MEM request directly and consume no additional cycle. With
an empty entry and a current ordinary-RAM store, drive that store on
the bus. If dmemReady is high, complete it without filling the entry;
otherwise capture it and complete it internally on that edge. An
occupied entry always owns the bus and retains exactly the same
address, data and byte enables until its write is accepted. If it
drains while another ordinary-RAM store is in MEM, capture that new
store into the entry and complete the new instruction simultaneously;
only the old store reaches the external bus on that edge. If occupied
and unable to drain, a new store holds in MEM. Never overwrite an
unaccepted entry, count an enqueue as a bus write, or replay a store
after its instruction has advanced.

Define ordinary RAM as the existing contract's entire address range
below 0x00100000, with the existing width/alignment checks. Every
address outside ordinary RAM remains unbuffered and ordered. In
particular, all MMIO requests wait for the entry to empty and then
complete only on their own external handshake. Apply this policy to
the whole address class, without recognizing benchmark marker PCs,
individual marker addresses, data values or workload phases. Preserve
out-of-bounds observability: an invalid address must still reach the
existing checker through the ordinary unbuffered request path, not
become a silently completed or discarded store.

Loads never bypass an occupied entry, even on the edge it drains:
hold the load while the old write owns the bus, then issue the load
on the following cycle. There is no associative lookup, load cache,
store-to-load forwarding or speculative load response. This preserves
ordering for all overlapping addresses and byte masks. While an entry
drains, ordinary non-memory instructions may complete normally. Make
accepted MISC-MEM fences and the existing EBREAK termination marker
wait until earlier writes have drained; a non-bus barrier may advance
on the edge that accepts the final pending write. Preserve their
existing architectural effects and decoder legality. EBREAK must not
end simulation with an externally unperformed, retired store pending.

Replace raw dmemReady-based global stalling with a MEM completion-wait
signal from this arbitration. A buffered store alone does not freeze
the pipeline. A current load, unbuffered access, barrier, or store
lacking buffer capacity does hold the appropriate MEM instruction.
Route this wait through the existing hazard priorities: EX/MEM and
ID/EX hold, PC holds, and MEM/WB clears only valid while retaining its
forwarding payload. Compute wait without feedback from those hold
outputs. The entry's external drain runs independently of MEM holds,
instruction-bus stalls, divider work and invalid pipeline bubbles.
Reset cancels its validity and suppresses stale external requests.
Enqueue requires the current valid, nontrapping store actually to
complete; wrong-path, illegal and misaligned instructions cannot enqueue.

Keep the MEM/WB RVFI payload tied to the completing instruction, never
to whichever older buffered transaction currently owns the bus. At
enqueue, a store records its original PC, instruction, forwarded raw
sources, aligned RVFI address, replicated write data and byte mask
exactly once. Later external draining emits no retirement and no
register-file write. Preserve contiguous rvfi_order, original load
response capture, traps, source forwarding and division acceptance
semantics. The real and ALTOPS arithmetic paths remain unchanged.

Estimate a three-percent fitness improvement, with low confidence.
Savings depend on stores being followed by useful non-memory work;
an immediately following load can consume the overlap, and the bus
ownership mux or completion controls may lower Fmax. Empty-buffer
fall-through preserves zero-wait latency, but does not establish a
timing gain. Inspect actual buffer state, request arbitration, mapped
area and all three routed critical paths, including the dmem address
and load-response paths. Compare exact marker-bracketed cycles on
identical workloads and stall settings. Improvement requires the
Fmax ratio to exceed the cycle-count ratio against the retained core,
whose measured fitness is 467.44 iterations/s; do not use rounded IPC.
