cosim and standard three-seed FPGA gates. Add independent transaction
scoreboards that distinguish instruction completion, queue capture,
and external write acceptance. Preserve every architectural assertion
and all canonical 6 KB CRC, validated-UART, address-bound, liveness

title: Condition-aware bias for the existing agree predictor
motivation:
The retained r4s2 winner uses 32 private two-bit counters to predict agreement
with the displacement sign. The predictor history in experiments/log.jsonl
shows that additional capacity, global history, shared hysteresis, private
Gray recoding, loop tracking, and polarity banking all lost fitness. The
r10s2 polarity-bank experiment reduced modeled errors but changed counter
allocation and lookup structure, then lost 26.04% fitness. A smaller remaining
opportunity is to improve the meaning of agreement while preserving the
winning table, PC hash, local update circuits, and training latency.

Replaying the archived r9s2 branch-event trace gives 47235 direction errors
for the current bias and 43017 for the proposed bias over 529588 conditional
branches inside the timing markers: 4218 fewer errors, about 8.93%. Both
models include all preceding warmup events and identical binary saturating
counters. The retained trace-source RTL matches the current bench RTL byte
for byte. This model updates in retirement order and omits fetch timing,
queued training, and candidate-dependent stalls; these are not measured
candidate cycles or Fmax. The trace is from the existing scored 2000-byte
ELF documented in prior implementation notes, distinct from the requested
supplemental 6000-byte validation. Neither workload nor evaluator may change.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one predictor-policy change: define a conditional branch's static
agreement bias as B = instruction[31] OR instruction[12]. Instruction bit
12 is funct3[0]. Thus legal BNE, BGE, and BGEU start with a taken bias in
either displacement direction; BEQ, BLT, and BLTU retain backward-taken,
forward-not-taken bias. Every branch can still learn the opposite direction.
This fixed instruction-based rule applies to all programs and addresses;
it uses no benchmark detection, PC-specific constants, or preloaded outcomes.

In IF, compute B from raw imem_data and use
branch_direction = B XOR !agree_msb. Keep legal-branch predecode, PC and
target alignment eligibility, the shared B/J target adder, and accepted
pred_taken handling exactly as they are. The extra OR and existing bias
inversion form a three-input Boolean function of instruction[31],
instruction[12], and agree_msb, which can fit in one LUT4; confirm actual
mapping rather than assuming that this preserves whole-core Fmax.

In EX, use the identical bias expression from the resolving instruction:
branch_train_agree = (branch_cond == (in.instr[31] | in.instr[12])).
Keep branch_train_valid's existing valid, legal, nontrapping, advancing-EX
qualification, including reset, dmem-hold, and divider-wait exclusions.
Use the fully forwarded actual branch condition, never pred_taken, to
generate this event. IF prediction and EX training must use the same rule.

Preserve branch_predictor.sv's binary counters and reset value 11, the
PC[6:2] XOR PC[11:7] index, all 32 private entries, MSB-only lookup, and
seven-bit registered training event. Pending events still drain exactly
once, reset cancels them, and lookup retains old-state semantics with no
training bypass. No new predictor state, banks, tags, history, ports, or
pipeline metadata are needed. JAL prediction, JALR fallback, EX recovery,
architectural pc_next, traps, memory behavior, and nret=1 RVFI remain intact.

Validate all six branch conditions, both displacement signs, and both actual
outcomes against an independent bias-and-counter model. Explicitly exercise
forward inverse-condition branches that agree and disagree with their new
cold taken bias, delayed learning through both direction changes, aliases,
accepted predictions across a counter update, reset, load-use forwarding,
dmem holds, and divider holds. Preserve wrong-path-store suppression, exact
retirement order and PC chaining, reserved-encoding and alignment traps,
and existing saturation/event-queue assertions. Rework directed stimuli
where their old bias assumptions no longer reach the intended state.

Run the unchanged correctness and FPGA fitness gates and the requested
6000-byte CRC/marker validation. Compare actual bracketed cycles and median
Fmax from all three prescribed routing seeds separately. The direction-model
improvement suggests only a small cycle opportunity; even a small Fmax loss
could erase it. The integer +1% fitness forecast is an optimistic, low-
confidence hypothesis, not a conversion of modeled errors into measured
throughput. No evaluation contract or other core is an editing target.

reset-to-11 policy, PC[6:2] XOR PC[11:7] hash, MSB-only lookup, seven-bit
registered event, old-counter acceptance, and exactly-once event draining
are unchanged. `branch_predictor.sv` and its standalone unit test are

history, banks, metadata, prediction bypasses, or workload-specific rules.

oracle derives bias semantically from the decoded condition and signed
branch displacement; it uses the existing independent arithmetic counter

qualification and agreement, pending events, all 32 counters, held payloads,
and accepted directions against the previous cycle. Retirement-side events
must exactly match EX events, with full unchanged ISS/RVFI comparison,
contiguous order, PC chaining and accepted memory transaction checks.

- All six legal conditions, both displacement signs, both actual outcomes,

  pending drains, reset cancellation, reserved branch/JALR encodings,
  misaligned transfers, wrong-path branch suppression and arithmetic tests.

and reuses them for four work clocks. The original sequential-divider
experiment, hyp-20260906-002-r1s1, improved fitness by 20.30 percent, but
its unrolling factor has not subsequently been tuned. Recent micro_opt
attempts to change ALU selection and register-file paths repeatedly lost
routed frequency, including r11s0's 34.43 percent regression. Reducing
the existing divider's combinational footprint is a distinct, localized
opportunity to reduce placement and routing pressure.

latency increase for that observed workload; it does not establish the

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Tune only the existing divider's spatial unrolling from eight binary
restoring steps to six. Execute five work clocks of six steps followed
by one final work clock of two steps: 5*6+2 = 32 quotient bits. Keep the
separate registered sign/exception correction in FINISH. A request then
receives response_valid exactly seven clocks after acceptance, compared
with five currently. This is a local arithmetic resource-sharing
micro-optimization within the existing unit and pipeline interfaces.

Construct a single six-step prefix chain from quotient_q, remainder_q,
and divisor_q, preserving the existing 33-bit trial remainder, unsigned
compare/subtract, and quotient-bit insertion at every step. Retain the
state after step two as a tap in that same chain. On work_q == 5 commit
that two-step tap and enter FINISH; otherwise commit the six-step result.
Do not execute 36 effective steps or build a separate two-step datapath.
Widen work_q to three bits and initialize it to zero on reset and request
acceptance. The final-tap mux and extra counter bit are the principal
added logic; two restoring stages should disappear from the work cone.

Preserve operand-magnitude capture, original RVFI operands, signed
truncation, dividend-signed remainder, divide-by-zero results, and
INT_MIN/-1 behavior. Keep IDLE/WORK/FINISH/RESPONSE, busy, held responses,
consume, and reset cancellation semantics. In RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS retain
the exact original captured-operand formulas and use the same six-work-
clock state schedule and seven-clock response as the real datapath.
The existing EX request/consume protocol, metadata capture, inert wait
bubbles, forwarding, and dmem-backpressure priority require no change.

With continuously ready buses, the existing pipeline is expected to
retire consecutive divides nine clocks apart, within the unchanged
ten-cycle liveness window. Verify that bound using dependent and
independent consecutive divisions and the existing formal gate; never
extend formal depths or bypass the real stall protocol under ALTOPS.
Keep all other instruction latencies, ALU operation decoding, multiplier
expressions and sharing, register file, predictor, nret=1, top-level IO,
trap discipline, and retirement ordering intact.

Estimate a three percent fitness gain through lower divider resource
use and improved whole-core routing, with low confidence. The current
routed bottleneck need not traverse the divider, and the final-tap mux
or remapping could erase the benefit. Confirm the six-stage shared
prefix structure in synthesis and report LUT4/FF/DSP use and all three

title: Separate memory address generation from the shared ALU result
motivation:
Every memory address currently passes through the general ALU operand
muxes, binary operation selection, jump-link override, and EX/MEM
divider-completion/bubble selection before driving the data bus. Loads
and stores only need the fully forwarded rs1 plus their immediate.
Sharing the architectural-result register with effective addresses also
couples register-result forwarding to address, alignment, and lane-mask
fanout. A dedicated address-generation lane can remove this unnecessary
selection from the memory path without adding a stage or changing IPC.

The structural history provides a specific reason to test this split.
The r2s1 multiplier pipeline and r10s1 registered result lanes failed to
remove remaining execute selection/qualification bottlenecks. The r11s1
store buffer saved only 0.83% of scored cycles and lost 10.63% fitness;
all three candidate critical paths ran from ID/EX ALU control to the
register driving dmem_addr[0]. That is evidence from a regressing
candidate, not proof that this is the retained winner's worst path:
the retained r4s2 reports instead end at ID/EX register-file operands.
The proposed resource split is therefore a low-confidence timing
experiment, with no assumed cycle saving or guaranteed Fmax gain.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one dedicated, registered effective-address lane parallel to the
existing EX ALU. Compute effective_addr_next = forwarded_rs1 + in.imm
with full 32-bit modulo arithmetic, directly from the existing resolved
rs1 and immediate. It must not use alu_a, alu_b, alu_result, the current
ALU opcode, jump-link selection, or the divider result mux. Register
this sum at the existing EX/MEM boundary; retain ordinary ALU results
and the current three-source forwarding network in their present form.
This is a structural separation of address generation from register
result generation, with no new pipeline stage or memory transaction.

Keep the address register outside the main EX/MEM whole-bundle update
and divider metadata registers. Its update is simply reset-to-zero,
otherwise hold on the existing EX/MEM data-memory stall, otherwise
capture the new sum. Do not put valid, memory-op, jump, div_wait, or
div_consume conditions on its data input or capture enable. It may
contain an irrelevant address during a bubble or non-memory operation;
the existing instruction controls continue to determine whether any
access occurs. Assemble this register into a new effective_addr field
of the outgoing EX/MEM bundle after the main bundle selection, using
one driver per signal. Do not reintroduce a divider/bubble address mux
by first storing the new field in reg_q or div_meta_q.

In MEM, make this effective_addr the sole address source for dmem_addr,
byte masks, halfword/word misalignment checks, load byte extraction,
and the word-aligned RVFI memory address. Keep the existing ALU result
exclusively on the register-result forwarding/writeback path. All
memory instruction metadata, forwarded raw source values, replicated
store data, masks, load responses, and retirement must still belong
to the same accepted instruction. Preserve trap-side suppression of
memory effects and register writes, and report zero RVFI memory address
and masks when the existing contract requires no access.

A stalled load or store holds both its main EX/MEM payload and its
separate address until the data bus accepts it. On that acceptance
edge MEM captures the old address with the old instruction, while EX
can capture the next instruction and its address. Divider work still
drains older MEM work once and inserts inert EX/MEM bubbles; free
address updates during those bubbles must never create a request.
Reset, wrong-path cancellation, load-use bubbles, imem backpressure,
and delayed MEM/WB forwarding retain their current behavior. Do not
add address truncation, benchmark-specific qualification, an address
whitelist, buffering, speculative loads, or a MEM-to-EX load bypass.

Preserve the decoder, predictor, register file, ALU arithmetic and its
real/ALTOPS branches, divider latency, hazard policy, and nret=1 port
and retirement contract. The intended cycle count is unchanged under
both zero-wait and identical randomized instruction/data stalls. The
forecast is a four-percent fitness gain from timing alone; extra adder
area, forwarding fanout, unchanged ALU/RF paths, or placement movement
may instead cause a regression. This estimate is not a measured result.

Validate forwarded base addresses from EX/MEM and MEM/WB, load-to-base
dependencies, positive and negative immediates, full-width carry and
wraparound, all load/store widths and lanes, and misaligned traps.
Exercise repeated data stalls, simultaneous instruction stalls,
consecutive memory operations, divide launch/completion adjacent to
accesses, redirect cancellation, and reset. Check accepted request
stability and counts, exact RVFI operands/addresses/masks/data, and
contiguous single retirement against the existing independent model.

Run the unchanged lint, cocotb, single-channel formal, stalled cosim,
and three-seed FPGA gates. Verify actual synthesis keeps a dedicated
address register/adder cone free of current-instruction ALU-result
selection and preserves the wrapper's memory inference. Inspect all
three routed critical paths, register-result timing, and area; do not
equate an isolated address-path improvement with a whole-core gain.
Use identical ELFs and marker-bracketed cycles for each comparison,
including the required 6000-byte CRC/UART validation. Keep any recorded
evaluator workload distinct from that supplemental contract check;
change no evaluator, workload, wrapper, or other core. Against the
retained 196.16 MHz result, improvement requires Fmax_new / 196.16 to
exceed cycles_new / cycles_retained on the same workload.

title: Carry-select target generation for aligned direct predictions
motivation:
The retained r4s2 winner already predicts direct transfers with a compact
32-entry agree table. The predictor records in experiments/log.jsonl show
that added capacity, history, loop tracking, and condition banking saved
little or no CoreMark time while losing routed frequency. Even r11s2's
two-expression bias change saved only 0.112% of scored cycles and lost
22.79% fitness. Preserving the winning prediction policy while shortening
its target-generation feedback path is a remaining predictor opportunity.

IF currently adds a sign-extended B/J immediate to the full 32-bit PC.
Prediction eligibility already establishes that the PC and target are
word aligned. Moreover, every B/J immediate has identical sign bits above
bit 20. Those facts permit a shorter low-address addition with parallel
upper-address adjustments, without a target table or additional state.
Prior worst paths were in EX, so this is a low-confidence physical-timing
hypothesis; a shorter fetch adder alone does not establish a fitness gain.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change only the existing direct predictor's target arithmetic in IF:
implement its shared B/J target as an aligned carry-select sum, retaining
the current immediate extraction, direction table, and prediction policy.
Keep the full 32-bit PC register and external addresses. This proposal
adds no lookup entries, tags, history, target cache, or pipeline stage.

Reuse pred_imm selected from the raw fetched B/J encoding. Form the
explicitly widened twenty-bit sum
  low_sum = {1'b0, pc[20:2]} + {1'b0, pred_imm[20:2]}.
Independently compute eleven-bit upper_same = pc[31:21],
upper_plus = pc[31:21] + 11'd1, and
upper_minus = pc[31:21] - 11'd1, with eleven-bit modular results.
Let S = pred_imm[31] and C = low_sum[19]. Select upper_plus for
{S,C}=2'b01, upper_minus for 2'b10, and upper_same for 00 or 11.
Assemble pred_target = {selected_upper, low_sum[18:0], 2'b00}.
Use explicit widths and parallel upper expressions so no upper increment
or decrement waits for the low carry; only their final selection does.

For every eligible direct prediction this equals the original full-width
PC-plus-immediate result modulo 2^32: the upper immediate is zero or
eleven ones, so the upper word changes by C-S. Both low address bits are
zero by existing eligibility. The proposal-stage software arithmetic
check matched full modular addition on 100064 boundary and random aligned
B/J-range vectors; this checks the formula, not synthesized RTL or timing.

Keep the existing legal BRANCH funct3 predecode, JAL recognition, aligned
PC requirement, and encoded target-bit-one checks unchanged. The assembled
target may be selected only when the existing raw_pred_taken is true;
ineligible encodings continue to select PC+4. Keep sequential PC+4 and EX
redirect_target arithmetic unchanged. In particular, preserve all upper
address bits and wrapping behavior; do not restrict targets to the FPGA
memory size or special-case benchmark PCs, offsets, or timing markers.

Preserve the binary agree counters, PC hash, reset-to-11 policy, seven-bit
queued training event, local saturating updates, and old-state lookup
semantics. Keep accepted pred_taken capture, hold/flush behavior, and EX
recovery priority over imem stalls intact. EX still computes architectural
targets, alignment traps, link data, and RVFI pc_next independently. No EX,
decoder, hazard, memory, divider, top-level interface, or nret change is
part of this hypothesis. All work is confined to cores/bench.

Check public fetch behavior against an independent full-width addition
oracle for both signs and extreme B/J immediates, low-sum carry/no-carry,
every upper selection, 2 MiB boundaries, and 32-bit wraparound. Use the IF
unit test for out-of-range synthetic addresses, keeping integrated memory
tests within the existing memory contract. Retain reserved-encoding and
misalignment tests, not-taken fallthrough, learned direction reversals,
wrong-path store suppression, and reset/recovery/stall priority checks.
Exercise accepted predictions and held metadata under imem backpressure,
dmem holds, load-use bubbles, and divider waits with exact retirement and
memory comparison. No existing correctness assertion may be weakened.

Run the unchanged lint, unit, formal, cosim, and three-seed FPGA gates.
Confirm whether synthesis preserves a nineteen-bit low addition and

title: Flatten EX/MEM transfer selection with mutually exclusive enables
motivation:
The retained execute stage wraps every normal result and its metadata in
a div_consume / div_wait / normal priority selection. The divide-wait
expression includes both operation recognition and response qualification,
so division control can affect ordinary EX/MEM capture timing even when
the executing instruction is not a divide.

The micro_opt history identifies a specific reason to isolate this outer
selection. In r9s0, replacing the ALU selector lost multiplier sharing;
r10s0 restored one MULT36X36 but still exposed divide-group control to
EX/MEM alu_result[1] as the routed bottleneck in two seeds. Folding the
jump override into the ALU in r11s0 instead exposed a long PC+4 path.
The r12s0 divider reduction saved area without improving timing or scored
cycles. These results motivate a local rewrite of transfer control while
retaining the existing ALU and divider datapaths. The incumbent's own
reported worst paths end in ID/EX, so a whole-core frequency gain remains
uncertain; this proposal does not claim the divider is its critical path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the priority selection feeding the EX/MEM register with a
parallel, two-source masked OR. Keep synchronous reset first and the
existing dmem stall hold second. On an actual non-reset, non-stalled
register update, use these two shared combinational enables:

  normal_enable = !is_div && !div_busy
  division_enable = div_valid

Construct a completed_division payload from div_meta_q, overriding its
alu_result with div_result exactly as the current div_consume arm does.
Form the entire next register payload as

  (next_ex & {$bits(ex_mem_t){normal_enable}}) |
  (completed_division & {$bits(ex_mem_t){division_enable}})

Both divider implementations define div_valid only in RESPONSE, whereas
div_busy is true in every state except IDLE. Thus div_valid implies
div_busy, and the two enables are mutually exclusive. On an update edge,
div_consume equals div_valid because reset and stall have already been
excluded. An idle ordinary instruction selects next_ex; an accepted or
working divide selects neither source and writes an entirely zero
EX/MEM bundle; RESPONSE selects the captured metadata and registered
arithmetic result. Reset still zeros the complete register, and stall
still holds every bit. Preserve this equivalence rather than allowing
arbitrary payload data in invalid bubbles.

This factors response and handshake qualification out of the normal
payload selection and gives each payload bit a two-product AND/OR form
that can fit a LUT4 after the shared enables are formed. Keep the hold
outside this merge, rather than adding the old register as another data
candidate. The intended benefit is less control depth and repeated logic
around the existing result boundary, with no additional registers or
instruction latency. Mapping may already perform some of this factoring;
reduced RTL nesting alone is not evidence of a speedup.

Keep is_div recognition, div_request, div_consume, div_wait, captured
forwarded operands, divider state transitions and five-clock response
latency unchanged. The original div_wait must still control frontend
holds, redirects and predictor training. Preserve next_ex generation,
jump-link selection, multiplier expressions and sharing, binary ALU
decoding, all ALTOPS formulas, raw-source RVFI values, memory side
effects, nret=1, and retirement ordering. In particular, retain the
existing assertion that the complete EX/MEM register is zero during
divider work; do not replace it with a valid-only check.

Estimate three percent higher fitness from Fmax alone, with low
confidence. Use the unchanged lint, cocotb, formal, stalled strict RVFI
cosim and three-seed FPGA gates. Compare exact marker-bracketed cycles
using identical retained and candidate ELFs and bus-ready sequences;
they should match. Report median routed Fmax against 196.16 MHz, fitness
against 467.44, all three critical paths, and LUT4/FF/DSP counts. Verify
that the mapped outer merge actually changes and one MULT36X36 remains.
Preserve the evaluator's scored workload and also validate the required
6 KB, -O3, ten-iteration run with both stalls, canonical CRCs, timing
markers, bounds and completion text. Modify no evaluation-contract file.

title: Move link and divider result selection beyond EX/MEM
motivation:
The current EX/MEM result D input combines normal ALU selection, the
PC+4 jump override, divider-response insertion, and whole-bundle bubble
clearing. Structural experiments r2s1 and r12s1 left ordinary ALU-control
paths critical despite changing multiplication or address generation.
In r10s0, even registered grouped ALU commands left divide-group and
is_jump paths through result/advance selection critical at 175.56 MHz.
The r10s1 four-lane experiment moved the final merge across EX/MEM, but
pre-register result qualification still connected target/trap logic to
a result-lane D input; its median was 173.13 MHz. These observations
motivate separating raw result capture from instruction-result ownership,
specifically removing link, division, and bubble selection from the
normal arithmetic register. The retained 196.16 MHz design also has RF
timing pressure, so this is a testable timing hypothesis, not a proven
improvement or evidence that the multiplier datapath needs pipelining.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace EX/MEM's single preselected result register with three parallel
raw 32-bit registers and a registered mutually exclusive result-source
tag at the SAME boundary: normal integer/multiply result, PC+4 link,
and divider response. Select the architectural result only from these
registered words and the registered tag. This is one structural retiming
of exceptional-result insertion and ownership. Keep the pipeline stage
count, every instruction latency, divider handshake, and retirement
boundary unchanged. Retain one normal ALU lane rather than expanding
individual integer operation classes into additional result registers.

Add an ALU raw_normal output containing exactly the existing ADD through
MULHSU operations. All these operation numbers are 0 through 14, so its
operation selection can use only op[3:0]; give the unused low-nibble
value a deterministic default. This output is meaningful architecturally
only for normal operations. DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU may produce arbitrary
deterministic raw_normal values because their normal lane is never
selected. Do not put a full-opcode legality or divide-class mask back
on this raw output. Keep the existing five-bit op interface, divider
connection, and standalone out behavior: valid normal opcodes select
raw_normal, divide opcodes select div_result, and unsupported opcodes
still return zero. EX consumes raw_normal directly; the compatibility
out is not on its synthesized result path. Preserve the existing real
multiply expressions and their mutually exclusive binary selection,
signed widths, every multiply ALTOPS formula, and all divider arithmetic
and ALTOPS behavior. No multiplier pipeline or new arithmetic algorithm
belongs to this change.

In EX, capture raw_normal, in.pc + 32'd4, and div_result into separate
registers. Each register resets to zero, holds on the existing EX/MEM
dmem-stall input, and otherwise captures on every clock. Do not qualify
their D inputs or capture enables with in.valid, opcode class, reg_write,
memory controls, jump/trap conditions, div_wait, or div_consume. The
normal ALU's intrinsic operation selection remains, but no completion,
bubble, or link override follows it before its register. The divider
lane likewise samples the response data directly; its registered tag
determines whether that sample belongs to a completing division.

Keep the existing metadata reset/hold/consume/bubble/normal priorities.
On normal advancement, register NORMAL or LINK ownership with the same
instruction; an invalid bubble receives no ownership. On div_consume,
restore the existing saved divide metadata and register DIV ownership.
During div_wait, clear ownership and clear valid plus every side-effect
control in the metadata after older work drains. A genuine dmem hold
preserves all raw registers, ownership, and metadata together. Reset
clears ownership and cancels pending state using the existing protocol.
A valid trapping instruction still retires with its existing trap and
suppressed effects; an irrelevant raw result never authorizes a write.

Retain ex_mem_t's external shape. Inside ex_stage, leave the alu_result
slot in next_ex, the main metadata register, and div_meta_q constant
zero, so none of those wide bundle muxes owns live result data. Assemble
out from the metadata and overwrite only out.alu_result with a balanced
selection of the three registered lanes using the registered one-hot
ownership bits; no ownership yields zero. Use a single combinational
driver for that assembly. This preserves the existing core, MEM and
forwarding interfaces. All dmem address, alignment, mask, extraction,
and RVFI-address consumers continue to use the same assembled result;
memory instructions select NORMAL. Do not add a separate address path.

The same assembled result feeds the existing EX/MEM bypass and MEM/WB
capture. Keep the three operand-source ages, youngest-writer priority,
load-use interlock, RF write-through, and retained MEM/WB forwarding
payload. Division must still capture fully forwarded original operands
and RVFI metadata exactly once before older writers drain, hold the
frontend during work, drain older MEM work once, and transfer its result
once on consumption. On that consumption edge the raw DIV register
samples the valid response while the matching saved metadata advances.
A younger consumer accepted on the same edge must see that completed
value through the ordinary EX/MEM forwarding path on the next cycle.
Preserve redirect/training timing and all imem/dmem stall priorities.

The forecast is five percent higher fitness from timing alone, with low
confidence. Costs include up to 64 additional raw result bits, ownership
bits, and a post-register selector on forwarding, address and MEM capture
paths. Those paths, unchanged normal ALU selection, RF timing, or placement
changes may outweigh removal of the old qualification chain. Confirm in
the mapped netlist that the raw normal register has no combinational
dependency on current op[4], div_wait, div_consume, jump-link selection,
or trap/valid qualification; distinguish ALU operand selection from the
removed result override. Confirm exactly one MULT36X36 remains and the
unmodified FPGA wrapper retains its memory inference. Inspect all three
routed critical paths and whole-core LUT4/FF/DSP counts; a local cone
improvement is not sufficient evidence of a fitness gain.

Extend the existing arithmetic and independent pipeline/RVFI checks for
normal-to-link-to-divide transitions, immediate consumers through both
bypass ages, load-use dependencies, competing destinations, x0, all
load/store widths, misaligned traps, and wrong-path effects. Exercise
repeated and overlapping bus stalls, divider acceptance/completion,
back-to-back divides, and reset cancellation. Check accepted memory
request stability/counts, original source operands, exact results,
contiguous single retirement, and unchanged directed retirement gaps.
Preserve every existing correctness assertion and exact arithmetic
vector; internal probes may be adapted to the new representation while
retaining the same behavioral guarantees. Raw inactive lanes may change
during bubbles, but externally assembled inert entries must remain inert.

Run unchanged lint, cocotb, single-channel ALTOPS formal, stalled cosim,
and three-seed FPGA gates. Use identical ELFs and bus-stall sequences
for retained/candidate comparisons; bracketed cycles should be identical.
Evaluate exact iterations/cycle rather than the rounded core.yaml IPC.
Against the retained result, improvement requires Fmax_new / 196.16 to
exceed cycles_new / cycles_retained. Prior implementation notes identify
a scored 2 KB ELF separately from the requested 6 KB contract validation;
preserve the actual evaluator workload and separately verify the 6 KB
d4b0/be52/5e47 CRCs, both MMIO timing markers, bounds checks, and the
literal Correct operation validated. Preserve nret=1, exact core ports,
default-illegal decoding, traps, liveness, and all other hard invariants.
Change no evaluator, wrapper, workload source, core.yaml, or other core.

title: Bias-sensitive indexing for the 32-entry agree predictor
motivation:
The retained r4s2 predictor reaches 467.44 iterations/s with 32 private
two-bit agree counters and queued local training. The predictor history
shows that larger tables, global history, shared confidence, condition
banks, and loop tracking produced small cycle benefits or regressions
while frequently losing substantial routed Fmax. The latest target-adder
change also lost frequency without changing cycles. A smaller remaining
opportunity is to change which branches interfere in the existing table.

The current PC-only hash maps forward and backward branches at colliding
PCs to the same counter regardless of their static bias. Agreement coding
makes many such collisions constructive, but not all: a branch that
persistently disagrees with its bias can disturb a colliding branch that
follows its bias. Folding that bias into the index changes these pairings
while preserving the existing agreement convention and counter capacity.

A proposal-stage replay of the retained r9s2 branch-event trace models
532346 legal branch events, including 529588 inside the timing markers.
With immediate retirement-order training, the retained index produces
47235 marked-region direction errors; XORing the static bias into index
bit 4 produces 46158, a reduction of 1077 (2.28% of modeled errors).
This is supporting evidence for one index change, not a measurement of
pipeline recoveries, CoreMark cycles, Fmax, or the requested 6 KB workload.
The trace came from the unchanged evaluator's archived 2 KB run.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change only conditional-branch table indexing. For the fetched branch,
define the five-bit index as
  pc[6:2] ^ pc[11:7] ^ {imem_data[31], 4'b0000}.
For the resolving branch, generate its training index as
  in.pc[6:2] ^ in.pc[11:7] ^ {in.instr[31], 4'b0000}.
Thus opposite displacement signs toggle the upper index bit for a given
PC hash. Every bias class can still use all 32 entries across PCs. This
is an XOR permutation of the existing hash, not a fixed sixteen-entry
allocation per class. It adds one Boolean XOR at lookup and training,
with no table expansion, tags, history, queue widening, or new metadata.

Preserve the current direction rule, imem_data[31] XOR NOT agree_msb,
and the training rule, branch_cond equals in.instr[31]. Do not adopt
r11s2's condition-aware bias or r10s2's funct3 banking. Retain all 32
binary counters, reset to 11, the seven-bit registered event, generated
constant-index saturating updates, and the MSB-only lookup. Keep the
predictor module interface and state representation unchanged. Apply
the lookup expression to raw imem_data, independently of flush, stall,
redirect, and the masked instruction sent to ID, as the present IF
predecode does. Do not add a second dynamically read counter or a
training-to-lookup bypass to implement the new hash.

Fetch and EX must use the PC and instruction belonging to their own
pipeline positions. EX can recompute the index from its already-held
PC and instruction because this hash contains no changing history.
Capture the accepted pred_taken exactly as today; a counter update or
change in live bus data must never revise a held instruction's saved
prediction. On an update edge, acceptance still sees the old counter
MSB. Drain a pending training event once even when no new event arrives,
and cancel it on reset. Preserve the existing valid, legal, nontrapping,
advancing-EX training qualification and all stall/recovery priorities.

Keep legal BRANCH funct3 recognition, alignment eligibility, JAL and
JALR behavior, the full-width B/J target adder, EX actual target and
direction resolution, architectural pc_next, traps, links, and memory
side effects unchanged. Counter collisions affect only speculation;
EX remains authoritative. Preserve nret=1 and every RVFI and evaluation
invariant. All implementation work is confined to cores/bench RTL and
its permitted cocotb tests.

Update the independent fetch and pipeline prediction oracles to include
the displacement sign in the index. Check that IF and EX select the same
entry for each accepted conditional branch. Cover both signs, all six
legal conditions, every index, same-sign PC collisions, opposite-sign
branches whose former collision is separated, and new collisions caused
by the XOR. Train both agreeing and disagreeing phases, including a
threshold-crossing update coincident with fetch acceptance. Preserve
exactly-once training, queued-event draining, reset cancellation,
wrong-path store suppression, legality/alignment traps, and exact ISS,
RVFI-order, PC-chain, and memory comparisons. Exercise imem stalls,
dmem holds, load-use bubbles, and divider waits. Change only expectations
that intentionally depend on the index, retaining architectural checks.

The +1% fitness estimate is an optimistic low-confidence target. The
replay omits fetch timing and queued updates, and its error reduction
cannot be substituted for saved cycles. A small frequency loss could
outweigh the entire benefit. Run the unchanged lint, unit, formal,
stalled cosim, and three-seed FPGA gates; report bracketed cycles and
median routed Fmax separately and compute fitness from the unrounded
iterations/cycle ratio. Inspect mapping to confirm unchanged predictor
state and local update structure, and check whether the added instruction
input worsens the lookup path or remaps unrelated critical paths.
Compare identical workloads and stall streams. Preserve the evaluator
as supplied and separately verify the requested 6 KB CRCs, timing
markers, completion literal, and memory bounds if the recorded workload
discrepancy persists. Do not edit workloads or evaluation-contract files.

implementation_notes:
Implemented the bias-sensitive index exactly as proposed. All local correctness
gates pass. The three-seed FPGA result is a regression: fitness is 411.36
iterations/s versus retained r4s2's 467.44 (-12.00%). The implementation is
left in place for the orchestrator's evaluation.

Only two RTL expressions change:

- IF uses `pc[6:2] ^ pc[11:7] ^ {imem_data[31], 4'b0000}`.
- EX uses `in.pc[6:2] ^ in.pc[11:7] ^ {in.instr[31], 4'b0000}`.

IF reads raw bus data regardless of masking, flush, stall, or recovery. EX
recomputes from its own held PC and instruction. The direction and agreement
rules are unchanged. The predictor module, its interface, 32 binary counters,
reset-to-11 policy, seven-bit event, constant-index local updates, MSB-only
lookup, old-state acceptance, and pending-event drain semantics are unchanged.
All remaining RTL is byte-for-byte unchanged, including the full-width target
adder, saved prediction metadata, qualification and recovery priorities,
decoder, traps, memory side effects, divider, and single-channel RVFI interface.
`core.yaml` remains unchanged with `nret: 1`.

There are no architectural deviations. The supplied evaluator still scores
2 KB CoreMark. The requested 6 KB workload was built and checked separately
from identical workload sources, using the existing Makefile parameters; no
workload or evaluation-contract file was edited or replaced.

The independent IF and pipeline prediction oracles now include the sign bit.
The standalone predictor test and transition oracle remain byte-for-byte
unchanged. Existing architectural checks were retained; index-dependent alias
addresses/expectations were updated to maintain their intended collisions.

IF coverage includes all 32 indices, both displacement signs, all six legal
conditions, same-sign PC aliases, formerly colliding opposite signs that now
separate, and newly colliding opposite signs. Both saturating training phases
are exercised. Each of the 768 MSB crossings in the exhaustive test coincides
with fetch acceptance and checks the old direction against the resulting PC.
Live raw sign changes under masking/stalls/recovery, queued-event draining,
reset cancellation, original legality/alignment checks, JAL/JALR handling,
full-width targets, and recovery priorities remain checked.

The pipeline scoreboard records the accepted branch's PC, instruction, index,
and prediction independently and checks all four against EX, including held
cycles. Every qualified EX event and its retirement-order correspondence are
checked exactly once, with every counter and queued event compared each cycle.
The expanded sweep runs 768 complete ISS comparisons: every index/sign/legal
condition under zero-wait and directed/random bus holds, with three same-sign
aliasing branch PCs and agreeing/disagreeing phases. It exercises 25,344 target
branch training events. The three sites follow a divider, a held store, and a
dependent load respectively. Unready imem data changes sign independently of
the held instruction. Separate tests retain threshold-crossing acceptance,
opposite-sign alias phases, both recoveries, wrong-path store/branch suppression,
pending-event draining during division, and reset cancellation for both signs.
Full ISS/RVFI comparisons, strict order, PC chaining, bus transaction counts,
memory bounds, and final ISS-memory equality all pass.

Local validation:

- Exact requested Verilator lint command: pass, no warnings or errors.
- Formal: pass on the first attempt, 53 passed / 0 failed; zero fix attempts.
  Ran `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=6 bash formal/run_all.sh`
  in an isolated scratch copy with unchanged script/configuration/framework.
  Automatic nret detection selected wrapper_si.sv and checks_si.cfg. This
  is the supplied ALTOPS gate; real arithmetic was covered by unit and cosim.
- All seven cocotb runners passed. Final XML results total 106 tests and zero
  failures, including four IF tests and 30 pipeline tests. The complete unit
  suite passed before the last two pipeline tests were added; the final
  pipeline runner then passed all 30 tests in 80.62 seconds.
- Unchanged cosim evaluator: pass, selftest plus stalled 2 KB CoreMark.
- Additional selftest runs with both stall flags and seeds 1, 22, 305419896:
  all 115 retirements match the unchanged ISS and retained RTL exactly.
  Respective final retirement cycles are 185, 177, and 193 for both cores.
- Unchanged synthesis and three-seed routing scripts/evaluator: all pass.
  The existing counter-array-to-register synthesis warning is expected.

Measured scored workload, ITERATIONS=10, identical ELF and default deterministic
`--istall --dstall` stream (seed 0xDEADBEEF):

| Metric | Retained r4s2 | Bias-sensitive index |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Bracketed 2 KB cycles | 4,196,463 | 4,194,828 |
| Start marker cycle | 14,996 | 15,053 |
| Stop marker cycle | 4,211,459 | 4,209,881 |
| Seed 1 routed Fmax, MHz | 196.16 | 157.46 |
| Seed 2 routed Fmax, MHz | 182.08 | 179.40 |
| Seed 3 routed Fmax, MHz | 201.25 | 172.56 |
| Median routed Fmax, MHz | 196.16 | 172.56 |
| Fitness, iterations/s | 467.44 | 411.36 |
| LUT4 | 6,146 | 6,139 |
| Flip-flops | 2,260 | 2,266 |

Cycles improve by 1,635 (-0.0389613825%), while median Fmax falls
12.0309951060%. Fitness uses the unrounded ratio:
`172.56e6 * (10 / 4194828) = 411.3637078802754` iterations/s.
The retained value is `196.16e6 * (10 / 4196463) = 467.44127137544166`.
The fitness change is -11.9967078068%. The evaluator's rounded
`ipc_coremark: 0.000002` was not used to recompute fitness. The proposal's
replay error improvement was not substituted for measured saved cycles.
Retained routed metrics come from the archived r4s2 gate; its complete RTL
was verified against current HEAD. Workload comparisons were rerun locally.

Mapping and timing inspection:

- Both mapped designs have exactly 64 DFFSE counter bits and seven DFFR
  event bits. Every counter D/enable cone terminates only at its own two
  bits and the registered event, with no other counter dependencies.
- The saved-prediction input cone reads all 32 MSBs, no counter LSBs, and
  no queued event bits. There is no second dynamic counter read or bypass.
- Training index bits 0-3 remain XOR LUT2s. Bit 4 changes from an XOR LUT2
  to a three-input XOR LUT3; event width remains five index bits.
- The longest mapped path from the instruction-sign source flop to saved
  prediction contains four logic cells versus five in the retained map.
  This is a structural depth comparison, not a routed-delay measurement.
  The added sign input is not on any reported final worst path.
- All three candidate worst paths start at `lfsr_DFFC_Q_10.Q`, representing
  instruction bit 20 / rs2 address bit 0, and end in ID/EX rs2 operand data.
  They are register-file selection paths, not the new sign/hash path:

| Seed | ID/EX endpoint | Logic ns | Routing ns |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | `cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_66.D`, rs2_val[29] | 2.78 | 3.57 |
| 2 | `cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_81.D`, rs2_val[14] | 2.78 | 2.80 |
| 3 | `cpu.u_id.reg_q_DFFRE_Q_71.D`, rs2_val[24] | 2.78 | 3.02 |

The retained worst paths also ended in ID operand capture, but originated in
MEM/WB bypass or register-file state. The two-expression change remaps unrelated
logic: the additional six mapped flops are named under EX (+4) and MEM (+2),
with no predictor-state growth. This measurement supports a whole-design
mapping/routing regression, not an isolated claim that the new XOR is the
critical path. The hypothesis does not meet its optimistic fitness target.

- The unchanged scored 2 KB ELF SHA-256 is
  `c2af1db144cd8fc7936f33f0a0e05a244938ebfc64c5fd362e5ffe88cde4a0d4`.
  Both runs pass the supplied 2 KB CRC evaluator, the exact completion

  Both cores ran this identical ELF and default stalled stream. Retained

  Applying the same measured median Fmax to the unrounded 6 KB ratios gives

  These are supplemental requested-workload results, not evaluator scores.
- Independently checked all requested 6 KB CRCs: crclist=d4b0,
  crcmatrix=be52, crcstate=5e47, plus seedcrc=8a02 and crcfinal=5949.
  Both report 10 iterations, the exact `Correct operation validated.`

`$TMPDIR/bias-index-verify.k6_s3u3j/`, including formal-gate.log, unit-gate.log,

title: Register fully qualified division control at ID/EX
motivation:
EX currently reconstructs division eligibility from five registered ALU
opcode bits, instruction validity, and legality. That result controls
div_request and div_wait, so its decode feeds frontend holds, recovery
qualification, and the EX/MEM bubble-versus-result decision even for
ordinary instructions. Moving this complete Boolean decision before the
existing ID/EX boundary could shorten a widely used control path with
only one additional state bit and no instruction latency change.

The micro_opt history repeatedly reports opcode-to-EX/MEM timing limits.
r9s0 combined division predecode with broad one-hot result selection and
inadvertently tripled multiplier resources. r10s0 preserved one multiplier
but still exposed division-related result control on routed critical
paths. r13s0 found that the outer payload merge already fit one LUT4.
This proposal isolates the upstream, fully qualified division decision;
it leaves the binary ALU, multiplier sharing, and existing result merge
intact. These are observations from prior candidates, not proof that
division recognition is the retained winner's worst routed path.

title: Retime link and divide selection with a direct registered memory path
motivation:
The retained execute-result register combines ordinary ALU selection,
jump-link insertion, divider completion, and bubble clearing. Prior
structural attempts r2s1 and r12s1 left ordinary ALU-control paths
critical; r10s1 retained qualification logic before its result registers.
The r13s1 raw normal/link/divide registers removed that qualification
and passed the recorded formal and cosim gates, but never produced a
routed fitness result. Its post-register result selector also drove
dmemAddr, preventing MEMORY_DFF from absorbing the address register.
The unchanged wrapper consequently mapped its memory to 1,024 RAM16SDP4
cells instead of four DPX9B blocks and failed placement.

This leaves a specific structural hypothesis untested: move exceptional
result selection across EX/MEM while preserving a direct registered
memory-address source. Unlike r12s1's separate address adder, the existing
raw normal-result register can supply that source at no additional
address-register cost. Removing the link/divide insertion chain might
improve execute timing without changing instruction latency. Retained
RF timing and the new forwarding selector remain substantial risks.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the single preselected EX/MEM result register with raw normal,
PC+4 link, and divider-response registers plus a registered one-hot
result-source tag, all at the existing EX/MEM boundary. Select the
register-write/forwarding result from those registered words. Expose
the raw normal register separately and connect it directly to every
memory-address consumer. These are the two necessary interfaces of
one structural retiming: register results before exceptional-result
selection, while keeping the memory read address directly registered.
Keep pipeline depth, instruction latency, retirement, fetch prediction,
and the existing three operand-source ages unchanged.

In alu.sv expose raw_normal for ADD through MULHSU. These operation
codes are 0 through 14, so use only op[3:0] for this output's selection,
with a deterministic default for the unused low-nibble value. Do not
feed the divider result, full-opcode validity, or a normal-class mask
into raw_normal. For divide or unsupported opcodes its value is unused
architecturally. Preserve the standalone five-bit out interface:
normal opcodes return raw_normal, DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU return div_result,
and unsupported opcodes return zero. Keep the existing multiply
expressions and binary exclusivity so synthesis can still share one
MULT36X36. Preserve every real and ALTOPS arithmetic formula and the
divider's existing request/response interface and completion latency.

In EX, raw_normal_q, raw_link_q, and raw_div_q reset to zero, hold on
the existing dmem stall, and otherwise sample raw_normal, PC+4, and
div_result on every clock. Their capture must not depend on valid,
result class, reg_write, memory controls, trap, div_wait, or div_consume.
Keep the existing metadata reset/hold/consume/bubble/normal priorities.
Register NORMAL or LINK ownership on a valid normal advancement and
DIV ownership with the restored saved metadata on div_consume; clear
ownership for bubbles and during divider work after older MEM drains.
Hold ownership and metadata together on dmem backpressure. Keep live
result data out of the metadata and saved divide bundles; assemble
out.alu_result after the raw registers from the registered ownership
bits, returning zero when no lane owns a result. Traps retain their
existing metadata and suppressed architectural effects.

Add a 32-bit internal EX output mem_addr_raw driven by raw_normal_q
itself, and wire it through core.sv into mem_stage. Do not create a
second address adder, a fourth result lane, or an extra pipeline stage.
Every decoded load/store uses the ordinary ADD operation with forwarded
rs1 and the I/S immediate, so raw_normal_q already holds its correct
full-width effective byte address on the matching MEM cycle. Use this
source for dmem_addr, byte-lane masks, misalignment detection, load
extraction, and the word-aligned RVFI memory address. Continue using
the assembled architectural result for EX/MEM forwarding and MEM/WB
alu_result capture. Keep mem_wb_t and the public core ports unchanged.

In particular, dmem_addr must be a direct wire from raw_normal_q, with
no result-source mux, opcode selection, ownership mask, valid-to-zero
mux, or added register between it and the bus. Non-memory cycles may
expose an irrelevant raw address; existing cleared memory controls
keep requests inactive. Preserve all current alignment/trap gating of
read enables and write masks. A waiting memory transaction must hold
its raw address, data, masks, and instruction metadata until accepted.
This direct register-to-address connection is the essential difference
from the placement-failed r13s1 design and must be verified in synthesis.

Preserve divide acceptance only after older MEM can advance, capture
fully forwarded original operands and RVFI metadata exactly once, hold
PC and ID/EX during work, and drain older work without replay. On the
consumption edge raw_div_q samples the valid response while DIV
ownership and saved metadata advance together. Immediate consumers
must receive that result through the existing youngest-writer-priority
bypass. Preserve load-use bubbles, RF write-through, held MEM/WB
forwarding data, reset cancellation, branch training, and redirect
priorities under overlapping imem/dmem stalls.

First inspect synthesis with the unchanged FPGA wrapper: require its
four DPX9B memory blocks and one MULT36X36 to remain, and verify that
the dmem address comes directly from the raw normal register. Inspect
the normal register's input cone for removal of op[4], link/divide
insertion, and result-ownership qualification; ordinary ALU operand
muxing and low-nibble operation selection are expected to remain.
Then run the unchanged lint, cocotb, single-channel ALTOPS formal,
stalled cosim, and three-seed FPGA gates. Preserve existing independent
arithmetic and RVFI assertions and add directed coverage for transitions
among normal, link, divide, and memory instructions, immediate consumers,
all memory widths, misaligned traps, x0, wrong-path effects, repeated
bus stalls, and reset. Check exact accepted request counts and stability
of held memory transactions as well as contiguous retirement order.

Expect identical bracketed cycles with identical ELFs and stall seeds;
any cycle difference needs explanation before attributing a timing gain.
Compare exact iterations/cycle and median routed Fmax against retained
196.16 MHz and 467.44 fitness, not the rounded core.yaml throughput.
Improvement requires Fmax_new / 196.16 > cycles_new / cycles_retained.
Report all three paths and LUT4/FF/DSP/BSRAM counts. The forecast is a
five-percent fitness improvement from timing, with low confidence:
approximately 64 extra result bits, the post-register bypass selector,
RF paths, or placement changes could outweigh the removed EX logic.

Prior experiment notes distinguish the evaluator's 2 KB ELF from its
supplemental canonical 6 KB run. Do not change the evaluator or workload
to reconcile them. Preserve apples-to-apples evaluator measurements and
separately verify the requested 6 KB crclist=d4b0, crcmatrix=be52,
crcstate=5e47, both MMIO timing markers, bounds checks, and the literal
Correct operation validated. Preserve nret=1, exact top-level ports,
decoder default-illegal and SYSTEM rules, all traps, bounded progress,
M-extension correctness, and every hard invariant. Modify only bench
RTL and its test/test_*.py suites during implementation.

title: Sixteen-entry tagged exception predictor for static branch bias
motivation:
The retained r4s2 winner uses 32 untagged agree counters. Every legal
conditional branch updates its hashed counter, so a branch following its
static bias can repeatedly erase a colliding branch's learned exception.
LESSONS.md and the predictor experiment records show that simply doubling
capacity in r5s2 saved only 0.14% of scored cycles, while global history,
shared hysteresis, condition banking, and bias-sensitive indexing failed
to improve fitness. The r8s2 counter recoding also lost frequency at
identical cycles. A remaining opportunity is selective allocation with
tags: retain training for exceptions and prevent unrelated, bias-following
branches from disturbing them.

Proposal-stage replay supports this specific mechanism on both workloads.
The archived 2 KB branch stream contains 529588 marked-region branches;
immediate retirement-order training gives 47235 direction errors for the
retained predictor and 41762 for the proposed table. A fresh streamed run
of the retained simulator on the archived 6000-byte ELF contains 3755488
legal branches, including 3747912 between the timing markers. The same
models give 354032 versus 291289 marked-region errors, a reduction of
62743, or 17.72%. That retained run completes with the requested d4b0,
be52, and 5e47 CRCs, the completion literal, and 30730562 bracketed cycles.
The retained RTL beside that simulator matches the current bench RTL.
The 6 KB ELF SHA-256 is

hypothesis.motivation:
The retained r4s2 winner uses 32 untagged agree counters. Every legal
conditional branch updates its hashed counter, so a branch following its
static bias can repeatedly erase a colliding branch's learned exception.
LESSONS.md and the predictor experiment records show that simply doubling
capacity in r5s2 saved only 0.14% of scored cycles, while global history,
shared hysteresis, condition banking, and bias-sensitive indexing failed
to improve fitness. The r8s2 counter recoding also lost frequency at
identical cycles. A remaining opportunity is selective allocation with
tags: retain training for exceptions and prevent unrelated, bias-following
branches from disturbing them.

Proposal-stage replay supports this specific mechanism on both workloads.
The archived 2 KB branch stream contains 529588 marked-region branches;
immediate retirement-order training gives 47235 direction errors for the
retained predictor and 41762 for the proposed table. A fresh streamed run
of the retained simulator on the archived 6000-byte ELF contains 3755488
legal branches, including 3747912 between the timing markers. The same
models give 354032 versus 291289 marked-region errors, a reduction of
62743, or 17.72%. That retained run completes with the requested d4b0,
be52, and 5e47 CRCs, the completion literal, and 30730562 bracketed cycles.
The retained RTL beside that simulator matches the current bench RTL.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the untagged agree table with one direct-mapped, sixteen-entry
tagged exception table. Preserve the existing backward-taken/forward-
not-taken bias, B/J target generation, and authoritative EX resolution.
The single architectural change is which branches own predictor state
and which training events may modify it.

Each entry contains a six-bit partial PC tag and a private two-bit binary
agreement counter C. Use index = PC[5:2] XOR PC[10:7] and tag = PC[11:6]
consistently at fetch and EX. These ten index/tag bits distinguish aligned
PCs within a 4 KB region; higher-address aliases remain possible and affect
prediction accuracy only. Counter value 11 also denotes an invalid entry,
eliminating a separate valid bit. Reset every counter to 11 and every tag
to zero. A valid matching entry predicts agreement when C[1] is one and
disagreement when C[1] is zero. A tag miss or invalid entry predicts
agreement with the static displacement-sign bias. Conditional direction
therefore remains instruction[31] XOR NOT agree_msb.

Consume the previous registered training event exactly once on each
nonreset clock. Let A be the resolving branch's actual agreement with
its own instruction[31], using the existing fully forwarded condition.
Update only the indexed entry according to this complete policy:
- If C is not 11 and its tag matches the event tag, increment C with
  saturation for A=1 and decrement C with saturation for A=0. Reaching
  11 invalidates the entry; its tag may remain stored but is ignored.
- On a tag miss or invalid entry with A=0, replace the tag and set C=10.
  This records the first exception while still predicting the bias;
  a subsequent matching disagreement moves 10 to 01 and enables the
  inverse prediction. Allocation must not immediately predict inverse.
- On a tag miss or invalid entry with A=1, leave both tag and counter
  unchanged. A bias-following nonowner cannot evict or strengthen an
  unrelated exception. Use no additional replacement or history policy.

Keep generated, constant-index sequential update blocks, each depending
only on its own state and the queued event. The event contains valid,
four index bits, six tag bits, and agreement: twelve registered bits.
Capture validity on every clock, drain an older event when a new event
is absent, and cancel pending training on reset. Preserve advancing,
valid, legal, nontrapping EX qualification, including dmem and divider
holds. Consecutive same-entry events must consume the newest local
counter state in order. There is no live EX-to-lookup training bypass.

Implement lookup as sixteen parallel inverse-hit terms, each requiring
its constant index, matching tag, and C[1]=0. Their OR means disagree;
its complement is agree_msb. This form needs no dynamic counter-LSB read,
full-word tag-read mux, or explicit C!=11 test on the prediction path.
The state budget is 128 entry bits plus twelve event bits, versus the
retained predictor's 64 plus seven: 69 additional bits. Measure mapped
area and timing; fewer entries do not imply a smaller or faster design.

IF derives index and tag from its current PC independently of flush,
stall, and masked instruction data. EX derives them from its own held
PC. Wire these internal fields through core without changing pipeline
bundles: the existing accepted pred_taken bit remains sufficient since
there is no history-dependent index or predicted indirect target. Fetch
acceptance on an update edge sees pre-edge prediction state. Holds must
preserve the saved prediction even when table ownership changes.
Preserve all branch legality/alignment checks, JAL/JALR behavior, shared
full-width target addition, recovery priorities, resolved pc_next, trap
and link behavior, memory effects, nret=1 ports, and every RVFI invariant.

Extend independent predictor, IF, and pipeline reference models for
ownership and allocation, retaining architectural assertions. Cover all
sixteen indices, all 64 tags, counter transitions, weak allocation,
deallocation, same-index conflicting owners, ignored agreeing misses,
and partial-tag aliases across 4 KB regions. Include consecutive events,
replacement or threshold crossings coincident with fetch acceptance,
queued-event draining and reset cancellation, both branch biases and all
legal conditions, wrong-path branches/stores, imem stalls, dmem holds,
load-use bubbles, and divider waits. Check accepted predictions and
exactly-once EX training against the matching retiring instructions;
preserve complete ISS/RVFI, order, PC-chain, trap, and memory comparisons.

The +1% estimate is an optimistic, low-confidence fitness target. Even
the modeled 6 KB error reduction is only about 0.20% of retained cycles
if each removed error saves one cycle, before pipeline/stall effects.
Tag comparison and additional state could lose more Fmax than that gain
permits, as prior predictor experiments demonstrate. Run unchanged lint,
cocotb, formal, stalled cosim, and three-seed FPGA gates; report bracketed
cycles, LUT4/FF counts, and median routed Fmax separately and calculate
fitness from unrounded iterations/cycle. Inspect the actual critical
paths, including unrelated remapping, rather than assuming lookup limits
timing. Use identical ELFs and stall streams for both cores. Prior notes
report that the supplied scoring path uses 2 KB: preserve that evaluator
and separately verify the requested 6 KB CRCs, markers, completion, and
memory bounds, labeling the workloads explicitly. Modify no benchmark,
wrapper, tool, constraint, invariant, or other core.

Implemented the sixteen-entry tagged exception predictor exactly as proposed. Local correctness gates pass, and the unchanged 2 KB evaluator measures a 1.4600412555% fitness improvement over the retained r4s2 RTL.

Each of the sixteen entries has a six-bit tag and binary two-bit counter. Counter 11 is invalid; matching owners saturate toward agreement or disagreement; agreement reaching 11 deallocates. Disagreeing misses replace at 10, while agreeing misses preserve both fields. Sixteen generated constant-index sequential blocks consume one previous registered event using each entry's current local state. The twelve-bit event is captured every nonreset clock and drains even when no new branch advances. Reset clears all tags, invalidates every counter, and cancels pending training.

Lookup is an OR of sixteen constant-index inverse-hit terms using the matching tag and only the counter MSB. Its complement feeds the unchanged displacement-sign bias conversion. IF derives index PC[5:2] XOR PC[10:7] and tag PC[11:6] directly from its PC; EX derives the same fields from held in.pc. The accepted pred_taken bit, legal/nontrapping advancing EX qualification, fully forwarded branch conditions, target arithmetic, recovery priorities, stalls, divider, memory effects, and nret=1 RVFI wiring are unchanged. There is no EX or queued-event lookup bypass and no extra replacement/history policy.

The independent model now tracks ownership and selective allocation. Predictor tests exhaust all 16 indices and 64 tags, all matching counter transitions, deallocation, ignored agreeing misses at every confidence, weak replacement, consecutive events, queue draining, reset cancellation, and high-PC aliases. IF tests exhaust the same index/tag space, both displacement signs, partial aliases, replacement and threshold changes on fetch acceptance, stalls/flush/recovery, legality/alignment, JAL/JALR, and full-width targets. Pipeline tests retain the complete unchanged ISS/RVFI comparator, strict order and PC-chain checks, traps, accepted bus transactions, and wrong-path memory assertions. title: Eliminate false load-use bubbles while completing raw RVFI operands late
motivation:
hazard_unit currently compares a load destination with both encoded source
fields of every fetched instruction. For OP-IMM, LOAD and JALR, bits 24:20
belong to an immediate, and LUI, AUIPC and JAL consume neither encoded
source. Matches in these fields unnecessarily insert a load-use bubble.
This is an untried interlock opportunity in the bench experiment history.

A source-aware comparison alone is insufficient: the unchanged ISS and
pipeline comparator require both raw encoded source addresses and their
pre-instruction register values, including architecturally unused fields.
The r6s0 experiment demonstrated late completion of such RVFI operands
from the preceding load's MEM/WB payload. Its real load-to-branch bypass
saved 1.87% of scoring cycles but lost 4.05% Fmax. Here the instruction
never needs the missing value to execute, so no memory-data or predicate
path into ALU operands, branch resolution or recovery is required.

Current r14s2 notes place the worst routed paths in RF-to-ID/EX logic;
earlier ALU, RF and result-retiming micro-optimizations often exposed much
slower EX paths. A small change to which instructions require an existing
bubble offers a direct cycle-saving mechanism without restructuring those
datapaths. Its benefit and placement sensitivity still require measurement.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the existing load-use interlock sensitive to actual operand use,
while completing any deferred, unused raw-source RVFI values at the
existing MEM/WB boundary. This is one interlock micro-optimization; retain
the pipeline depth, instruction latencies, RF read/write timing, ALU,
divider, branch predictor, external handshakes and nret=1 port contract.

Give hazard_unit the current IF/ID instruction in addition to its existing
source fields. Derive uses_rs1 and uses_rs2 combinationally from that same
offered instruction, independently of the resulting stall/accept signals.
Default both to one. Only for positively validated OP-IMM instructions,
LOAD funct3 in {0,1,2,4,5}, and JALR funct3=0, clear uses_rs2. OP-IMM
validation must preserve the existing shift funct7 restrictions. For
LUI, AUIPC and JAL, clear both. Keep both set for all other encodings,
including OP/M-extension, STORE, BRANCH, SYSTEM, MISC-MEM and illegal or
reserved neighbors. This small whitelist deliberately retains conservative
behavior outside the specified classes and does not change decoder legality.

The interlock becomes id_ex_mem_read && id_ex_rd!=0 &&
((uses_rs1 && id_ex_rd==if_id_rs1) ||
 (uses_rs2 && id_ex_rd==if_id_rs2)). A simultaneous genuine source match
must still stall, even if the other raw field is unused. Preserve every
existing dmem/divider hold, imem bubble, load-use flush and redirect
priority. Do not gate actual register reads or zero unused source addresses.

Preserve the full raw-source trace by adding exactly two deferred-source
flags to ex_mem_t. Wire the older EX/MEM load's valid/mem_read status and
destination into EX. When an ordinary instruction advances from EX,
independently mark each nonzero raw source that matches that immediately
older load. With the revised interlock, such a simultaneous match must be
an unused source of a whitelisted instruction; directed assertions must
verify this condition. Capture flags with the instruction, hold them under
dmem backpressure and clear them with bubbles/reset. A real DIV/REM uses
both sources and cannot acquire a deferred-source flag; preserve the
divider metadata capture and response protocol without new timing rules.

Exclude EX/MEM loads from ordinary EX/MEM data forwarding: their ALU
result is an address, not register data. Keep the existing three operand
candidates and EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB priority for eligible producers. Keep
retained MEM/WB forwarding even when its valid bit has been cleared by
a dmem hold. This gives each flagged source the correct old-register
fallback if the immediately older load traps instead of writing rd.
All true load consumers still wait for the normal MEM/WB bypass.

On the flagged instruction's normal MEM/WB capture, substitute the old
MEM/WB read_data for each flagged rs1_val/rs2_val only if the old payload
describes a nontrapping load with reg_write set, a nonzero destination,
and a matching raw source address. Use the pre-edge reg_q payload, not
the incoming instruction or current dmem bus word. Do not require the
old payload's valid bit: a following independent memory instruction can
itself stall in MEM, clearing that bit while retaining the older load's
data and controls for exactly this purpose. A faulting older load must
leave the ordinary forwarded fallback unchanged. Support both flags
together and preserve the encoded source addresses without modification.

This completion changes only the RVFI source-value payload, never the
architectural result, store data, branch condition, predictor training,
PC, memory transaction, register write or retirement timing. Keep all
alignment traps, strict order increments, wrong-path suppression and
decoder default-illegal checks. Inspect synthesis to establish whether
the RVFI-only flags and completion muxes disappear in the FPGA wrapper;
do not assume their area or timing cost is zero without checking.

Add directed pipeline cases for every whitelisted class, both raw fields
and simultaneous matches, all load widths/lanes and sign extensions,
x0, genuine dependencies, and reserved encodings. A false-only dependency
at zero wait must retire back-to-back with its older load; a true load-use
dependency must retain the existing bubble. Check complete raw-source
RVFI against the unchanged ISS, using poisoned prior destination values
and load data that differ from the effective address. Include a prior
writer followed by a misaligned load to the same rd, simultaneous unused
matches, younger independent loads/stores held in MEM, dmem holds before
pair advancement, imem stalls, prediction recovery, wrong-path effects,
divider waits and resets. Retain all architectural/order/PC-chain/memory
assertions; update only timing expectations intentionally changed by this
hypothesis and add explicit assertions for the new timing.

Expect an optimistic 1% fitness gain, with low confidence: no dynamic
count of removable bubbles has yet been measured, and opcode qualification
or changed forwarding enables may hurt Fmax. Run the unchanged lint,
cocotb, formal, stalled cosim and three-seed FPGA gates. Measure eliminated
false-only bubbles, marker-bracketed cycles, LUT4/FF counts and median
routed Fmax separately, using identical ELFs and stall seeds. Confirm
existing DSP and wrapper BRAM inference. The proposed gain is falsified
if Fmax loss outweighs the measured cycle savings.

Compute fitness from unrounded 10/bracketed_cycles against the retained
474.27 result. Prior r14s2 evidence identifies its 4,191,107-cycle scoring
binary as 2 KB, and the separate requested 6 KB binary as 30,665,846
bracketed cycles. Preserve the evaluator and report these workloads
separately. Validate the requested 6 KB CRCs d4b0/be52/5e47, markers,
completion literal and memory bounds on the same archived binary for
both implementations. Modify no benchmark, tool, wrapper, constraint,
contract, core.yaml value or other core.
